title.zh: 卷一百三十三 列傳第二十一 廖永安 俞通海 胡大海 耿再成 張德勝 趙德勝 桑世傑 茅成 胡深 孫興祖 曹良臣 濮英
title.en: Volume 133 Biographies 21: Liao Yongan, Yu Tonghai, Hu Dahai, Geng Zaicheng, Zhang Desheng, Zhao Desheng, Sang Shijie, Mao Cheng, Hu Shen, Sun Xingzu, Cao Liangchen, Pu Ying
title.raw: 卷一百三十三 列傳第二十一 廖永安 俞通海 胡大海 耿再成 張德勝 趙德勝 桑世傑 茅成 胡深 孫興祖 曹良臣 濮英 Volume 133 Biographies 21: Liao Yongan, Yu Tonghai, Hu Dahai, Geng Zaicheng, Zhang Desheng, Zhao Desheng, Sang Shijie, Mao Cheng, Hu Shen, Sun Xingzu, Cao Liangchen, Pu Ying

sentences.zh: 廖永安

translations.literal: Liao Yongan
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yongan

sentences.zh: 廖永安，字彥敬。

translations.literal: Liao Yongan, courtesy name Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yongan, whose courtesy name was Yanjing,

sentences.zh: 德慶侯永忠兄也。

translations.literal: He was the elder brother of Yongzhong, Marquis of Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: was the elder brother of Liao Yongzhong, later enfeoffed as Marquis of Deqing.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起，永安兄弟偕俞通海等以舟師自巢湖來歸。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor first rose, the Yongan brothers together with Yu Tonghai and others brought their fleet from Chaohu Lake to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the earliest days of the founding emperor's rise, the Yongan brothers came over from Chaohu Lake with Yu Tonghai and others, leading a naval force.

sentences.zh: 太祖親往收其軍，遂以舟師攻元中丞蠻子海牙於馬場河。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor went in person to take over their army, then used the fleet to attack the Yuan Vice Censor-in-Chief Balutu Haiya at Machang River.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor went in person to incorporate their forces, then sent the fleet against the Yuan vice censor-in-chief Balutu Haiya at Machang River.

sentences.zh: 元人駕樓船，不利進退，而永安輩操舟若飛，再戰，再破元兵，始定渡江策。

translations.literal: The Yuan men rode tower ships, ill suited for advance and retreat, while Yongan and his fellows handled their boats as if flying; fighting twice, they twice defeated the Yuan troops, and only then was the strategy for crossing the Yangzi settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan forces relied on tower ships, which were awkward to maneuver, whereas Yongan and his comrades handled their vessels like flying craft. After two engagements they twice routed the Yuan navy, and the plan to cross the Yangzi was at last fixed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，發江口。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, they set out from the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the fleet weighed anchor at the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 永安舉帆，請所向，命直指牛渚。

translations.literal: Yongan raised sail and asked where they should head; he was ordered to steer straight for Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yongan hoisted sail and asked for a heading; he was told to make straight for Niuzhu.

sentences.zh: 西北風方驟，頃刻達岸。

translations.literal: A northwest wind suddenly sprang up, and in an instant they reached the shore.
translations.idiomatic: A stiff northwest wind suddenly rose, and within moments they were ashore.

sentences.zh: 太祖急揮甲士鼓勇以登，採石鎮兵皆潰，遂乘勝取太平。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor urgently waved armored troops to rouse their courage and board; the garrison at Caishi all fled, and they pressed the victory to take Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor urgently ordered armored troops ashore with drums beating to hearten them; the Caishi garrison broke and fled, and the army pressed on to seize Taiping.

sentences.zh: 授管軍總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director-General of Troop Management.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director-general in charge of troop management.

sentences.zh: 以舟師破海牙水柵，擒陳兆先，入集慶。

translations.literal: With the fleet he broke Haiya's river palisade, captured Chen Zhaoxian, and entered Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the fleet he smashed Haiya's river blockade, took Chen Zhaoxian prisoner, and entered Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 擢建康翼統軍元帥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Marshal of the Jiankang Wing Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to marshal of the Jiankang wing command.

sentences.zh: 以舟師從取鎮江，克常州，擢同僉江南行樞密院事。

translations.literal: With the fleet he followed in the capture of Zhenjiang and the reduction of Changzhou, and was promoted to Associate Administrator of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the fleet in taking Zhenjiang and capturing Changzhou, and was promoted to associate administrator of the Jiangnan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又以舟師同常遇春自銅陵趨池州。

translations.literal: Again with the fleet he joined Chang Yuchun in marching from Tongling toward Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Again with the fleet he joined Chang Yuchun in advancing from Tongling toward Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 合攻，破其北門，執徐壽輝守將，遂克池州。

translations.literal: They attacked together, broke the north gate, seized Xu Shouhui's defending general, and thus took Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In a joint assault they breached the north gate, captured Xu Shouhui's defending general, and took Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 偕俞通海拔江陰之石牌戍，降張士誠守將欒瑞。

translations.literal: Together with Yu Tonghai he ascended the Shibai garrison on the Yangzi at Jiangyin and induced Zhang Shicheng's defending general Luan Rui to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu Tonghai he took the Shibai garrison on the Yangzi at Jiangyin and induced Zhang Shicheng's defender Luan Rui to submit.

sentences.zh: 擢同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又以舟師破士誠兵於常熟之福山港。

translations.literal: Again with the fleet he defeated Zhang Shicheng's troops at Fushan Harbor in Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Again leading the fleet he routed Zhang Shicheng's forces at Fushan Harbor in Changshu.

sentences.zh: 再破之通州之狼山，獲其戰艦以歸。

translations.literal: He defeated them again at Langshan in Tongzhou and returned with their warships as prizes.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Langshan in Tongzhou and returned with captured warships.

sentences.zh: 遂從徐達復宜興，乘勝深入太湖。

translations.literal: He then followed Xu Da in recovering Yixing and, pressing the victory, penetrated deep into Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Xu Da in recovering Yixing and, riding the momentum, pushed deep into Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 遇吳將呂珍，與戰。

translations.literal: He encountered the Wu general Lü Zhen and gave battle.
translations.idiomatic: There he met the Wu general Lü Zhen and fought him.

sentences.zh: 後軍不繼，舟膠淺，被執。

translations.literal: The rear did not follow up; his boat ran aground in the shallows and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The rear guard failed to keep up, his boat grounded in the shallows, and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 永安長水戰，所至輒有功。

translations.literal: Yongan excelled at naval warfare and wherever he went he invariably achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yongan was a master of naval combat and won distinction wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 士誠愛其才勇，欲降之，不可，為所囚。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng admired his talent and valor and wished to win him over, but he would not submit and was kept prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng admired his talent and courage and tried to win him over, but Yongan refused to submit and remained a captive.

sentences.zh: 太祖壯永安不屈，遙授行省平章政事，封楚國公。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor admired Yongan's unyielding spirit and conferred on him from afar the post of Branch Secretariat Grand Councillor and enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor honored Yongan's refusal to yield by conferring on him from afar the title of branch secretariat grand councillor and enfeoffing him as Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 永安被囚凡八年，竟死於吳。

translations.literal: Yongan was held prisoner for eight years in all and ultimately died in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yongan remained a prisoner for eight years and ultimately died in Wu territory.

sentences.zh: 吳平，喪還，太祖迎祭於郊。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, his coffin was returned and the Founding Emperor went out to the suburbs to receive and offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu was pacified, his coffin was brought home, and the founding emperor went out beyond the city to receive it and offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，帝念天下大定，諸功臣如永安及俞通海、張德勝、耿再成、胡大海、趙德勝、桑世傑皆已前沒，猶未有諡號，乃下禮部定議。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu, the Emperor reflected that the realm was largely settled, yet meritorious ministers such as Yongan, Yu Tonghai, Zhang Desheng, Geng Zaicheng, Hu Dahai, Zhao Desheng, and Sang Shijie had all died earlier and still lacked posthumous titles; he therefore ordered the Ministry of Rites to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year six, reflecting that the realm was at last largely settled, the emperor noted that founding ministers such as Yongan, Yu Tonghai, Zhang Desheng, Geng Zaicheng, Hu Dahai, Zhao Desheng, and Sang Shijie had all died without posthumous titles and ordered the Ministry of Rites to propose them.

sentences.zh: 議曰：「有元失馭，四海糜沸。

translations.literal: The deliberation stated: "The Yuan lost the reins of government and the four seas seethed.
translations.idiomatic: Their memorial read: "The Yuan had lost control of the realm and the four seas boiled with disorder.

sentences.zh: 英傑之士，或起義旅，或保一方，泯泯棼棼，莫知所屬。

translations.literal: Heroic men either raised righteous armies or held a region, in endless confusion, not knowing whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Heroic men raised armies or held their own territories in endless confusion, with no one to whom they might rally.

sentences.zh: 真人奮興，不期自至，龍行而雲，虎嘯而鳳。

translations.literal: The True Man rose in vigor, arriving unbidden; where the dragon moves, clouds follow; where the tiger roars, the phoenix comes.
translations.idiomatic: Then the true sovereign arose in power, coming unbidden as if by heaven's will—where the dragon moves, clouds gather; where the tiger roars, the phoenix answers.

sentences.zh: 若楚國公臣永安等，皆熊羆之士、膂力之才，非陷堅沒陣，即罹變捐軀，義與忠俱，名耀天壤。

translations.literal: Such men as the Duke of Chu, subject Yongan, were all warriors like bears and tigers, men of physical strength; if they did not break through hard defenses and perish in the ranks, they met calamity and gave their lives; righteousness and loyalty went together, and their names shine between heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Duke of Chu Yongan were warriors of bearlike strength; whether they fell storming enemy lines or perished in sudden disaster, they united righteousness with loyalty, and their fame shines across heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 陛下混一天下，追維舊勞，爵祿及子孫，烝嘗著祀典。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has unified the realm, looked back to old services, extended ranks and stipends to descendants, and established their seasonal offerings in the sacrificial canon.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has unified the realm, honored their past service, extended ranks and stipends to their descendants, and enrolled their seasonal sacrifices in the state ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 易名定諡，於禮為宜。

translations.literal: To change their names and fix posthumous titles is fitting in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: To grant them posthumous names and titles is what ritual propriety requires.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按諡法：以赴敵逢難，諡臣永安武閔；

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully applies the posthumous canon: for meeting the enemy in hardship, posthumously title subject Yongan Wu Min;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully applies the posthumous canon: for meeting the enemy amid hardship, Yongan should receive the posthumous title Wu Min;

sentences.zh: 殺身克戎，諡臣通海忠烈；

translations.literal: for giving his life in overcoming the foe, posthumously title subject Tonghai Zhong Lie;
translations.idiomatic: for giving his life in overcoming the enemy, Tonghai should receive Zhong Lie;

sentences.zh: 奉上致果，諡臣張德勝忠毅；

translations.literal: for serving the sovereign and achieving results, posthumously title subject Zhang Desheng Zhong Yi;
translations.idiomatic: for serving the sovereign and achieving decisive results, Zhang Desheng should receive Zhong Yi;

sentences.zh: 勝敵致強，諡臣大海武庄；

translations.literal: for defeating the enemy and bringing strength, posthumously title subject Dahai Wu Zhuang;
translations.idiomatic: for defeating the enemy and strengthening the state, Hu Dahai should receive Wu Zhuang;

sentences.zh: 辟土斥境，武而不遂，諡臣再成武壯；

translations.literal: for opening territory and pushing borders, martial but not completed, posthumously title subject Zaicheng Wu Zhuang;
translations.idiomatic: for opening territory and extending the borders, though martial achievement was left unfinished, Geng Zaicheng should receive Wu Zhuang;

sentences.zh: 折衝禦侮，壯而有力，諡臣趙德勝武桓。

translations.literal: for repelling the foe and resisting insult, stalwart and powerful, posthumously title subject Zhao Desheng Wu Huan.
translations.idiomatic: for repelling the enemy and resisting aggression, stalwart and powerful, Zhao Desheng should receive Wu Huan.

sentences.zh: 臣世傑，業封永義侯，與漢世祖封寇恂、景丹相類，當即以為諡。

translations.literal: Subject Shijie had already been enfeoffed as Marquis of Eternal Righteousness, comparable to Emperor Guangwu of Han enfeoffing Kou Xun and Jing Dan; his title should serve directly as his posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Shijie had already been enfeoffed as Marquis of Eternal Righteousness, comparable to how Emperor Guangwu of Han enfeoffed Kou Xun and Jing Dan; that title should serve directly as his posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」九年皆加贈開國輔運推誠宣力武臣、光祿大夫、柱國。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year all were further granted the titles Founding Assistant in Transporting Destiny, Promoting Sincerity and Displaying Merit Martial Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: " In year nine all were further granted the titles Founding Assistant in Transporting Destiny, Promoting Sincerity and Displaying Merit Martial Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 已，又改封永安鄖國公。

translations.literal: Later Yongan was again enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yongan was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 無子，授其從子升為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger cousin Sheng was appointed Assistant Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; his younger cousin Sheng was appointed assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 俞通海

translations.literal: Yu Tonghai
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tonghai

sentences.zh: 俞通海，字碧泉。

translations.literal: Yu Tonghai, courtesy name Biquan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tonghai, whose courtesy name was Biquan,

sentences.zh: 其先濠人也，父廷玉徙巢。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Hao; his father Tingyu moved to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: came of a family originally from Hao; his father Tingyu had moved to Chao.

sentences.zh: 子三人，通海、通源、淵。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Tonghai, Tongyuan, and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu had three sons: Tonghai, Tongyuan, and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元末，盜起汝、潁。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, bandits rose in Ru and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan, bandit armies rose in the Ru and Ying region.

sentences.zh: 廷玉父子與趙普勝、廖永安等結寨巢湖，有水軍千艘。

translations.literal: Tingyu, father and sons, with Zhao Pusheng, Liao Yongan, and others established a stockade at Chaohu Lake and had a fleet of a thousand vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu and his sons joined Zhao Pusheng, Liao Yongan, and others in fortifying Chaohu Lake, where they maintained a fleet of a thousand vessels.

sentences.zh: 數為廬州左君弼所窘，遣通海間道歸太祖。

translations.literal: They were repeatedly harassed by Zuo Junbi of Luzhou and sent Tonghai by a secret route to return to the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly harried by Zuo Junbi of Luzhou, they sent Tonghai by a secret route to join the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 太祖方駐師和陽，謀渡江，無舟楫。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was then encamped at Heyang, planning to cross the Yangzi, but had no boats.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was then encamped at Heyang, planning to cross the Yangzi but lacking any fleet.

sentences.zh: 通海至，大喜曰：「天贊我也！

translations.literal: When Tonghai arrived, he rejoiced greatly and said: "Heaven aids me!
translations.idiomatic: When Tonghai arrived, he exclaimed in delight: "Heaven is aiding me!

sentences.zh: 」親往撫其軍。

translations.literal: " He went in person to reassure their army.
translations.idiomatic: " He went in person to rally their forces.

sentences.zh: 而趙普勝叛去。

translations.literal: But Zhao Pusheng had already defected and left.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhao Pusheng had already defected and departed.

sentences.zh: 元兵以樓船扼馬場河等口。

translations.literal: Yuan troops used tower ships to block the mouths at Machang River and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan forces used tower ships to block the river mouths at Machang and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 瀕湖惟一港可通，亦久涸。

translations.literal: Along the lake shore only one harbor could be used, and it had long been dry.
translations.idiomatic: Along the lakeshore only one harbor remained passable, and it had long been dry.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，水深丈余，乃引舟出江，至和陽。

translations.literal: Then heaven sent great rain; the water rose more than a zhang, and they were able to lead their boats out to the river and reach Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Then heavy rain fell; the water rose more than ten feet, and they were able to lead the fleet out onto the Yangzi and reach Heyang.

sentences.zh: 通海為人沉毅，治軍嚴而有恩，士樂為用。

translations.literal: Tonghai as a man was deep and resolute; he governed the army strictly yet with kindness, and the troops were glad to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai was deep and resolute by nature; he commanded with strict discipline tempered by kindness, and his men served him gladly.

sentences.zh: 巢湖諸將皆長於水戰，而通海為最。

translations.literal: The Chaohu generals were all skilled in naval warfare, and Tonghai was foremost among them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaohu commanders were all skilled in naval warfare, but Tonghai stood foremost among them.

sentences.zh: 從破海牙諸水寨，授萬戶。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking Haiya's river stockades and was appointed Commander of Ten Thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in breaking Haiya's river stockades and was appointed commander of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，克採石，取太平，徇下諸屬縣。

translations.literal: He followed in the crossing of the Yangzi, captured Caishi, took Taiping, and swept the subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Yangzi crossing, captured Caishi, took Taiping, and swept through the surrounding counties.

sentences.zh: 海牙復以戰艦截採石，而陳兆先合淮兵二十萬屯方山，相犄角。

translations.literal: Haiya again used warships to block Caishi, while Chen Zhaoxian joined two hundred thousand Huai troops at Fangshan in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Haiya again blocked Caishi with warships while Chen Zhaoxian massed two hundred thousand Huai troops at Fangshan, the two positions supporting each other.

sentences.zh: 通海與廖永安等擊之，大敗其眾，海牙遁。

translations.literal: Tonghai with Liao Yongan and others attacked them, greatly defeated their host, and Haiya fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai and Liao Yongan attacked them, inflicted a crushing defeat, and Haiya fled.

sentences.zh: 進破兆先，取集慶路。

translations.literal: Advancing, they broke Zhaoxian and took the Jiqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing forward they defeated Zhaoxian and took the Jiqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 從湯和拔鎮江，遷秦淮翼元帥。

translations.literal: He followed Tang He in taking Zhenjiang and was transferred to Marshal of the Qinhuai Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Tang He in taking Zhenjiang and was appointed marshal of the Qinhuai wing.

sentences.zh: 偕諸將取丹陽、金壇、常州。

translations.literal: Together with other generals he took Danyang, Jintan, and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With other generals he captured Danyang, Jintan, and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷行樞密院判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從克寧國，下水陽，因以舟師略太湖，降張士誠守將於馬跡山，艤舟胥口。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Ningguo, descended to Shuiyang, then with the fleet raided Lake Tai, induced Zhang Shicheng's defending general to surrender at Maji Mountain, and moored at Xukou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in taking Ningguo, descended to Shuiyang, then raided Lake Tai with the fleet, induced Zhang Shicheng's defender to surrender at Maji Mountain, and anchored at Xukou.

sentences.zh: 呂珍兵暴至，諸將欲退。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen's troops suddenly arrived and the generals wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen's forces suddenly appeared, and the other generals wanted to retreat.

sentences.zh: 通海曰：「不可，彼眾我寡，退則情見。

translations.literal: Tonghai said: "It cannot be done; they are many and we are few—if we retreat our weakness will show.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai said: "We cannot. They outnumber us; if we retreat we reveal our weakness.

sentences.zh: 不如擊之。

translations.literal: Better to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: We should attack instead.

sentences.zh: 」乃身先疾斗，矢下如雨，中右目，不能戰。

translations.literal: " He then led the charge in person; arrows fell like rain and he was struck in the right eye and could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: " He led the charge himself. Arrows fell like rain; he was struck in the right eye and could no longer fight.

sentences.zh: 命帳下士被己甲督戰。

translations.literal: He ordered a man of his staff to don his armor and direct the battle.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a subordinate to don his armor and direct the battle in his place.

sentences.zh: 敵以為通海也，不敢逼，徐解去。

translations.literal: The enemy thought it was Tonghai and did not dare press close, and slowly drew off.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy believed it was Tonghai himself and did not dare press the attack, and gradually withdrew.

sentences.zh: 由是一目遂眇。

translations.literal: From this one eye was thereafter blind.
translations.idiomatic: From that wound he was blind in one eye for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 已，偕永安等克石牌戍，奪馬馱沙而還。

translations.literal: Later, together with Yongan and others, he took the Shibai garrison, seized horses and grain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Yongan and others, he took the Shibai garrison, seized horses and grain, and returned.

sentences.zh: 普勝既叛歸友諒，陷池州，遣別將守，而自據樅陽水寨。

translations.literal: Pusheng having defected to Youliang, took Chizhou, left a separate general to hold it, and himself occupied the Zongyang river stockade.
translations.idiomatic: After Pusheng defected to Chen Youliang, he seized Chizhou, left a deputy to hold it, and himself occupied the Zongyang river stockade.

sentences.zh: 太祖方征浙東，以樅陽為憂。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was then campaigning in eastern Zhe and was troubled by Zongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was campaigning in eastern Zhe and worried about the Zongyang stockade.

sentences.zh: 通海往攻，大破之。

translations.literal: Tonghai went to attack and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai attacked and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 普勝陸走，盡獲其舟，遂復池州。

translations.literal: Pusheng fled by land; they captured all his boats and thus recovered Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pusheng fled overland; they captured his entire fleet and recovered Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Associate Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒犯龍灣，偕諸將擊走之，追焚其舟於慈湖，擒七帥，逐北至採石。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang invaded Longwan; together with other generals Tonghai drove him off, pursued and burned his boats at Cihu, captured seven commanders, and chased him north to Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang invaded Longwan, Tonghai and other generals drove him off, pursued and burned his fleet at Cihu, captured seven commanders, and chased him north as far as Caishi.

sentences.zh: 功最，進樞密院同知。

translations.literal: His merit was foremost and he was advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His merit ranked first, and he was promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從攻友諒，下銅陵，克九江，掠蘄、黃。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Youliang, reduced Tongling, captured Jiujiang, and raided Qi and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Youliang, took Tongling, captured Jiujiang, and raided Qi and Huang.

sentences.zh: 從徐達擊叛將祝宗、康泰，復南昌。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in striking the rebel generals Zhu Zong and Kang Tai and recovering Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in suppressing the rebel generals Zhu Zong and Kang Tai and recovering Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 從援安豐，敗士誠兵。

translations.literal: He followed in the relief of Anfeng and defeated Zhang Shicheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Anfeng and defeated Zhang Shicheng's forces.

sentences.zh: 還攻廬州。

translations.literal: On the return he attacked Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he attacked Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 友諒大舉圍南昌。

translations.literal: Youliang raised a great force to besiege Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang then raised a large army to besiege Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 從太祖擊之。

translations.literal: Tonghai followed the Founding Emperor to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai followed the founding emperor to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 遇於康郎山，舟小不能仰攻，力戰幾不支。

translations.literal: They met at Kanglang Mountain; their boats were small and could not attack upward; fighting fiercely they nearly could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: They met at Kanglang Mountain. Their boats were too small to attack the enemy's towering vessels from below, and after fierce fighting they nearly broke.

sentences.zh: 通海乘風縱火焚其舟二十余，敵少挫。

translations.literal: Tonghai, riding the wind, set fire and burned more than twenty of their boats; the enemy was somewhat checked.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai used the wind to set fire to more than twenty enemy vessels, and the enemy's momentum faltered.

sentences.zh: 太祖舟膠，友諒驍將張定邊直前，犯太祖舟。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor's boat ran aground; Youliang's fierce general Zhang Dingbian pressed straight forward and assailed the Founding Emperor's boat.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor's boat ran aground. Youliang's fierce general Zhang Dingbian pressed forward and attacked his vessel directly.

sentences.zh: 常遇春射中定邊，通海飛舸來援，舟驟進水涌，太祖舟得脫。

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun shot and hit Dingbian; Tonghai came in swift boats to aid; the boat suddenly advanced as the water surged, and the Founding Emperor's boat escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun shot Dingbian; Tonghai raced up in swift boats to rescue him. The water suddenly surged, the boat lurched forward, and the founding emperor escaped.

sentences.zh: 而通海舟復為敵巨艦所壓，兵皆以頭抵艦，兜鍪盡裂，僅免。

translations.literal: But Tonghai's boat was again pressed by the enemy's great ships; the soldiers all braced their heads against the hull and their helmets were all cracked; he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai's own boat was then crushed by enemy great ships; his men braced their heads against the hull until their helmets cracked, and he barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，偕廖永忠等以七舟置火藥，焚敵舟數百。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; together with Liao Yongzhong and others they used seven boats loaded with gunpowder and burned several hundred enemy boats.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again. With Liao Yongzhong and others, seven boats loaded with gunpowder burned several hundred enemy vessels.

sentences.zh: 逾二日，復以六舟深入。

translations.literal: After two more days they again sent six boats deep into the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later six more boats penetrated deep into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 敵連大艦力拒。

translations.literal: The enemy linked great ships and resisted with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy linked their great ships and resisted with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 太祖登舵樓望，久之無所見，意已沒。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ascended the stern tower to look; after a long while he saw nothing and thought they had perished.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor climbed to the stern tower to watch. For a long time he saw nothing and assumed the boats had been lost.

sentences.zh: 有頃，六舟繞敵艦出，飄颻若游龍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the six boats emerged circling the enemy ships, drifting like swimming dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the six boats emerged from behind the enemy line, weaving through the fleet like swimming dragons.

sentences.zh: 軍士歡噪，勇氣百倍，戰益力。

translations.literal: The soldiers shouted for joy; their courage increased a hundredfold and they fought all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: The troops erupted in cheers; their courage redoubled and they fought with renewed fury.

sentences.zh: 友諒兵大敗。

translations.literal: Youliang's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's army suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 師次左蠡，通海進曰：「湖有淺，舟難迴旋。

translations.literal: The army halted at Zuoli; Tonghai advanced and said: "The lake has shallows and boats are hard to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Zuoli, Tonghai advised: "The lake has shallows where boats cannot maneuver freely.

sentences.zh: 莫若入江，據敵上流。

translations.literal: Better to enter the river and hold the enemy's upper stream.
translations.idiomatic: We should enter the Yangzi and hold the upstream position against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 彼舟入，即成擒矣。

translations.literal: When their boats enter, they can be captured at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once their fleet enters the river, we can take them at will.

sentences.zh: 」遂移師出湖，水陸結柵。

translations.literal: " They then moved the army out of the lake and built palisades on land and water.
translations.idiomatic: " The army was moved out of the lake, and palisades were erected on land and water alike.

sentences.zh: 友諒不敢出。

translations.literal: Youliang did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang did not dare venture out.

sentences.zh: 居湖中一月，食盡，引兵突走，竟敗死。

translations.literal: After a month on the lake their food was exhausted; he led his troops in a desperate breakout and ultimately was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped on the lake for a month until provisions ran out, he led a desperate breakout and was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 是役也，通海功最多。

translations.literal: In this campaign Tonghai's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign Tonghai's merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜良田金帛。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was granted fertile fields, gold, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was rewarded with fertile land, gold, and silks.

sentences.zh: 明年從平武昌。

translations.literal: The next year he followed in the pacification of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took part in pacifying Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 拜中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand councillor of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 總兵略劉家港，進逼通州，敗士誠兵，擒其將硃瓊、陳勝。

translations.literal: Commanding troops he raided Liujia Harbor, pressed toward Tongzhou, defeated Zhang Shicheng's army, and captured his generals Zhu Qiong and Chen Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In command of the army he raided Liujia Harbor, pressed toward Tongzhou, routed Zhang Shicheng's forces, and captured his generals Zhu Qiong and Chen Sheng.

sentences.zh: 進攝江淮行中書省事，鎮廬州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to act as Administrator of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat and garrisoned Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to administer the Jianghuai branch secretariat and garrisoned Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 從徐達平安豐。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in pacifying Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in pacifying Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 又從克湖州，略太倉。

translations.literal: Again he followed in the capture of Huzhou and raided Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed in capturing Huzhou and raiding Taicang.

sentences.zh: 秋毫不犯，民大悅。

translations.literal: Not a hair of the people was harmed and the populace rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: His troops did not harm a single civilian, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 圍平江，戰滅渡橋。

translations.literal: Besieging Pingjiang, he fought at Miedu Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Pingjiang he fought at Miedu Bridge.

sentences.zh: 搗桃花塢，中流矢，創甚，歸金陵。

translations.literal: Raiding Taohua Dock, he was struck by an arrow midstream; his wound was severe and he returned to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: While raiding Taohua Dock he was struck by an arrow; badly wounded, he returned to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 太祖幸其第，問曰：「平章知予來問疾乎？

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor visited his residence and asked: "Grand Councillor, did you know I came to inquire after your illness?
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor visited his home and asked: "Grand Councillor, did you know I came to inquire after your health?

sentences.zh: 」通海不能語。

translations.literal: " Tonghai could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Tonghai could not answer.

sentences.zh: 太祖揮涕而出。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor wiped away tears and left.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor wiped away his tears and left.

sentences.zh: 翼日卒，年三十八。

translations.literal: The next day he died, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next day, aged thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨哭甚哀，從官衛士皆感涕。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor came in person to mourn and wept bitterly; attending officials and guards were all moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor came in person to mourn and wept bitterly; officials and guards alike were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 追封豫國公，侑享太廟，肖像功臣廟。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yu, granted secondary sacrifice in the Grand Temple, and his portrait was placed in the Temple of Meritorious Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Duke of Yu, granted secondary sacrifice in the imperial ancestral temple, and his portrait installed in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，改封虢國公，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Guo with the posthumous title Zhong Lie.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year three he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Guo with the posthumous title Zhong Lie (Loyal and Ardent).

sentences.zh: 通海父廷玉官僉樞密院事，先卒，追封河間郡公。

translations.literal: Tonghai's father Tingyu had held the post of Associate Director of the Secretariat and died earlier; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai's father Tingyu, who had served as associate director of the secretariat, had died earlier and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 通海無子，弟通源嗣其官。

translations.literal: Tonghai had no son; his younger brother Tongyuan succeeded to his office.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghai had no son; his younger brother Tongyuan succeeded to his post.

sentences.zh: 弟 通源

translations.literal: Younger brother Tongyuan
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Tongyuan

sentences.zh: 通源，字百川。

translations.literal: Tongyuan, courtesy name Baichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tongyuan, whose courtesy name was Baichuan,

sentences.zh: 從大將軍征中原，偕副將軍馮勝等會兵太原，定河中。

translations.literal: He followed the Grand General in the campaign in the Central Plain, joined Vice General Feng Sheng and others at Taiyuan, and pacified Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the grand general in the Central Plain campaign, joined Vice General Feng Sheng at Taiyuan, and pacified Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 渡河，克鹿台，取鳳翔、鞏昌、涇州，守開城。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he took Lutai, captured Fengxiang, Gongchang, and Jingzhou, and garrisoned Kaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Yellow River, he took Lutai, captured Fengxiang, Gongchang, and Jingzhou, and garrisoned Kaicheng.

sentences.zh: 會張良臣據慶陽再叛，大將軍命諸將分兵蹙之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Liangchen held Qingyang and rebelled again, the Grand General ordered the generals to divide their forces and press in on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Liangchen rebelled again from Qingyang, the grand general ordered his commanders to converge on him from all sides.

sentences.zh: 通源自臨洮疾趨至涇，略其西，顧時略其北，傅友德略其東，陳德略其南。

translations.literal: Tongyuan rushed from Lintao to Jing and raided the west; Gu Shihui raided the north; Fu Youde the east; Chen De the south.
translations.idiomatic: Tongyuan rushed from Lintao to Jing and attacked from the west; Gu Shihui from the north; Fu Youde from the east; and Chen De from the south.

sentences.zh: 大將軍逼城下，良臣援絕糧盡，敗死。

translations.literal: The Grand General pressed the city; Liangchen's relief was cut off and provisions exhausted; he was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general pressed the city until Liangchen's relief was cut off and provisions exhausted; he was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 遂克慶陽。

translations.literal: Qingyang was thus taken.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyang was then captured.

sentences.zh: 征定西，克興元，皆先登。

translations.literal: Campaigning in Dingxi, he captured Xingyuan; in each case he was first over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dingxi campaign he captured Xingyuan, always being first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封南安侯，歲祿千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an with an annual stipend of fifteen hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year three he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an with an annual stipend of fifteen hundred piculs and granted a hereditary patent of investiture.

sentences.zh: 四年從廖永忠伐蜀，又從徐達出塞，撫甘肅，有功。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Liao Yongzhong in the Shu campaign, then followed Xu Da beyond the frontier, pacified Gansu, and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he followed Liao Yongzhong against Shu, then joined Xu Da beyond the frontier to pacify Gansu, winning distinction.

sentences.zh: 徙江南豪民十四萬田鳳陽。

translations.literal: He relocated one hundred forty thousand wealthy families of Jiangnan to farm at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated one hundred forty thousand wealthy families from Jiangnan to farm at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 又攻雲南，征廣南蠻，俘斬數萬。

translations.literal: Again he attacked Yunnan and campaigned against the Guangnan tribes, capturing and killing tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked Yunnan and campaigned against the Guangnan tribes, capturing and killing tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 二十二年詔還鄉，賜鈔五萬，置第於巢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year an edict ordered him home; he was granted fifty thousand notes and a residence was established for him at Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two he was ordered home, granted fifty thousand paper notes, and given a residence at Chao.

sentences.zh: 未行，卒。

translations.literal: Before he could depart, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, he died.

sentences.zh: 子祖，病不能嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zu was ill and could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zu was too ill to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 逾年，追論胡黨，以通源死，不問，爵除。

translations.literal: The next year, in the review of Hu Weiyong's faction, because Tongyuan was already dead he was not prosecuted, but the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the purge of Hu Weiyong's faction, Tongyuan was already dead and went unpunished, but the title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 弟 淵

translations.literal: Younger brother Yuan
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Yuan

sentences.zh: 胡大海

translations.literal: Hu Dahai
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dahai

sentences.zh: 胡大海，字通甫，虹人。

translations.literal: Hu Dahai, courtesy name Tongfu, a man of Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dahai, whose courtesy name was Tongfu, was a native of Hong.

sentences.zh: 長身、鐵面，智力過人。

translations.literal: Tall in stature, with an iron face, his strength and intelligence surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and broad-faced, with a countenance like iron, and his strength and intelligence surpassed ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 太祖初起，大海走謁滁陽，命為前鋒。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor first rose, Dahai hurried to pay his respects at Chuyang and was appointed vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor first rose, Dahai hurried to join him at Chuyang and was appointed vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，與諸將略地，以功授右翼統軍元帥，宿衛帳下。

translations.literal: He followed in the crossing of the Yangzi, with other generals seized territory, and for merit was appointed Marshal of the Right Wing Command and guarded the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Yangzi crossing, joined other generals in seizing territory, and for his merit was appointed marshal of the right wing and served as a guard at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 從破寧國，副院判鄧愈戍之。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Ningguo; Vice Director Deng Yu garrisoned it with him.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in capturing Ningguo, which Vice Director Deng Yu garrisoned alongside him.

sentences.zh: 遂拔徽州，略定其境內。

translations.literal: He then took Huizhou and pacified its interior.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Huizhou and pacified the surrounding region.

sentences.zh: 元將楊完者，以十萬眾來攻，大海戰城下，大破走之。

translations.literal: The Yuan general Yang Wanzhe came to attack with a hundred thousand men; Dahai fought below the walls and greatly defeated and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan general Yang Wanzhe attacked with a hundred thousand men; Dahai met him below the walls, inflicted a crushing defeat, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 遂與鄧愈、李文忠自昱嶺關攻建德。

translations.literal: He then with Deng Yu and Li Wenzhong attacked Jiande from Yuling Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Deng Yu and Li Wenzhong in attacking Jiande from Yuling Pass.

sentences.zh: 敗元師於淳安，遂克建德。

translations.literal: He defeated the Yuan army at Chun'an and thus took Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Yuan army at Chun'an and captured Jiande.

sentences.zh: 再敗楊完者，降溪洞兵三萬人。

translations.literal: He again defeated Yang Wanzhe and induced thirty thousand stream-and-cave troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Yang Wanzhe and induced thirty thousand tribal troops to surrender.

sentences.zh: 進樞密院判官。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 克蘭溪，從取婺州，遷僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: He captured Lanxi, followed in the taking of Wuzhou, and was transferred to Associate Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Lanxi, took part in capturing Wuzhou, and was promoted to associate director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 下諸暨，守將宵遁。

translations.literal: He reduced Zhuji; the defending general fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zhuji; the defending general fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 萬戶沈勝既降復叛，大海擊敗之，生擒四千餘人。

translations.literal: The Commander of Ten Thousand Shen Sheng had surrendered but rebelled again; Dahai defeated him and took more than four thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Shen Sheng had surrendered but rebelled again; Dahai defeated him and took more than four thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 改諸暨為諸全州。

translations.literal: Zhuji was renamed Zhuju Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuji was renamed Zhuju Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 移兵攻紹興，再破張士誠兵。

translations.literal: He moved his army to attack Shaoxing and again defeated Zhang Shicheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He moved against Shaoxing and again routed Zhang Shicheng's forces.

sentences.zh: 太祖以寧、越重地，召大海使守之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, because Ning and Yue were vital regions, summoned Dahai to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ning and Yue were strategically vital, the founding emperor recalled Dahai to guard them.

sentences.zh: 士誠將呂珍圍諸全，大海救之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng's general Lü Zhen besieged Zhuju; Dahai went to its relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng's general Lü Zhen besieged Zhuju; Dahai marched to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 珍堰水灌城，大海奪堰，反灌珍營。

translations.literal: Zhen dammed water to flood the city; Dahai seized the dam and in turn flooded Zhen's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen dammed the water to flood the city; Dahai seized the dam and redirected the flood against Zhen's camp.

sentences.zh: 珍勢蹙，於馬上折矢誓。

translations.literal: Zhen's position grew desperate; on horseback he broke an arrow in oath.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Zhen broke an arrow on horseback to swear an oath.

sentences.zh: 請各解兵，許之。

translations.literal: He asked that both sides withdraw their troops, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that both sides withdraw, and Dahai agreed.

sentences.zh: 郎中王愷曰：「珍猾賊，不可信，不如因擊之。

translations.literal: Attendant Wang Kai said: "Zhen is a cunning bandit and cannot be trusted; better to strike him while we can.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Wang Kai urged: "Zhen is a cunning enemy and cannot be trusted. We should attack him now.

sentences.zh: 」大海曰：「言出而背之，不信；

translations.literal: " Dahai said: "To speak and then go back on it is faithless;
translations.idiomatic: " Dahai replied: "To give one's word and then break it is faithless;

sentences.zh: 既縱而擊之，不武。

translations.literal: to release him and then attack is unwarlike.
translations.idiomatic: to let him go and then attack is unworthy of a warrior.

sentences.zh: 」師還，人皆服其威信。

translations.literal: " When the army returned, all admired his prestige and good faith.
translations.idiomatic: " When the army withdrew, all admired his integrity and authority.

sentences.zh: 尋攻處州，走元將石抹宜孫，遂定處州七邑。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he attacked Chuzhou, drove off the Yuan general Shimo Yisun, and thus settled the seven districts of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he attacked Chuzhou, drove off the Yuan general Shimo Yisun, and pacified all seven districts of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒寇龍江，命分軍搗信州，以牽制敵。

translations.literal: When Chen Youliang raided Longjiang, Dahai was ordered to detach troops and strike toward Xinzhou to pin down the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang raided Longjiang, he was ordered to detach troops and strike toward Xinzhou to pin down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 大海用王愷言，親引兵往，遂克信州，以為廣信府。

translations.literal: Dahai adopted Wang Kai's counsel, led the army in person, and thus took Xinzhou, which was made Guangxin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wang Kai's advice, Dahai led the army in person, captured Xinzhou, and established it as Guangxin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 信方絕糧，或勸還師。

translations.literal: Xinzhou had just run out of grain and some urged withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions in Xinzhou were exhausted, and some urged withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 大海曰：「此閩、楚襟喉地也，可棄之乎？

translations.literal: Dahai said: "This is the strategic throat of Fujian and Chu—can we abandon it?
translations.idiomatic: Dahai said: "This is the strategic gateway between Fujian and Chu. How can we abandon it?

sentences.zh: 」築城浚隍以守之。

translations.literal: " He built walls and deepened the moat to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: " He built walls, deepened the moat, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 先是，軍糧少，所得郡縣，將士皆征糧於民，名曰寨糧。

translations.literal: Earlier, army provisions were scarce; in counties taken, officers and soldiers all levied grain from the people, called stockade grain.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, army provisions were scarce, and in conquered counties officers and soldiers levied grain from civilians under the name "stockade grain."

sentences.zh: 民甚病之。

translations.literal: The people suffered greatly from this.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered greatly under this practice.

sentences.zh: 大海以為言，始命罷去。

translations.literal: Dahai spoke on their behalf, and only then was it ordered abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai reported this to the throne, and only then was the practice abolished.

sentences.zh: 進江南行省參知政事，鎮金華。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Administrator of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and garrisoned Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice administrator of the Jiangnan branch secretariat and garrisoned Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 初，嚴州既下，苗將蔣英、劉震、李福皆自桐廬來歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Yanzhou was taken, the Miao generals Jiang Ying, Liu Zhen, and Li Fu had all come to submit from Tonglu.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzhou fell, the tribal generals Jiang Ying, Liu Zhen, and Li Fu had submitted from Tonglu.

sentences.zh: 大海喜其驍勇，留置麾下。

translations.literal: Dahai was pleased with their valor and kept them under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai admired their fighting spirit and kept them in his service.

sentences.zh: 至是，三人者謀作亂，晨入分省署，請大海觀弩於八詠樓。

translations.literal: At this time the three plotted rebellion; in the morning they entered the branch secretariat and invited Dahai to view crossbows at the Eight Odes Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Now the three plotted rebellion. In the morning they entered the branch secretariat and invited Dahai to inspect crossbows at the Eight Odes Tower.

sentences.zh: 大海出，英遣其黨跪馬前，詐訴英過。

translations.literal: When Dahai came out, Ying sent his followers to kneel before his horse and falsely accuse Ying of faults.
translations.idiomatic: As Dahai emerged, Ying sent his men to kneel before his horse and falsely accuse Ying of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 大海未及答，反顧英。

translations.literal: Before Dahai could answer, he turned to look at Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Before Dahai could respond, he turned to look at Ying.

sentences.zh: 英出袖中槌擊大海，中腦僕地。

translations.literal: Ying drew a mallet from his sleeve and struck Dahai; it hit his brain and he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ying drew a mallet from his sleeve and struck Dahai on the head; he fell dead.

sentences.zh: 並其子關住、郎中王愷皆遇害。

translations.literal: Together with his son Guanzhu and Attendant Wang Kai, all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guanzhu and Attendant Wang Kai were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 英等大掠城中，奔於吳。

translations.literal: Ying and the others plundered the city greatly and fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and his men plundered the city and fled to Wu territory.

sentences.zh: 其後，李文忠攻杭州，杭人執英以降。

translations.literal: Later, when Li Wenzhong attacked Hangzhou, the people of Hang seized Ying and surrendered him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Wenzhong attacked Hangzhou, the townspeople seized Ying and handed him over.

sentences.zh: 太祖命誅英，刺其血以祭大海。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered Ying executed and his blood drawn to sacrifice to Dahai.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor ordered Ying executed and his blood used in sacrifice to Dahai.

sentences.zh: 大海善用兵，每自誦曰：「吾武人，不知書，惟知三事而已：不殺人，不掠婦女，不焚毀廬舍。

translations.literal: Dahai was skilled in the use of troops and would recite to himself: "I am a military man and know no books; I know only three things: do not kill people, do not seize women, do not burn dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai was a skilled commander who often said: "I am a soldier who knows no books; I observe only three rules: do not kill civilians, do not seize women, and do not burn homes.

sentences.zh: 」以是軍行遠近爭附。

translations.literal: " Because of this, wherever his army marched, near and far, people vied to join him.
translations.idiomatic: " Because of this, people near and far flocked to his banner wherever his army marched.

sentences.zh: 及死，聞者無不流涕。

translations.literal: When he died, none who heard of it failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death spread, all who heard wept.

sentences.zh: 又好士，所至輒訪求豪雋。

translations.literal: He also loved scholars and wherever he went would seek out eminent men.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved men of talent and wherever he went sought out eminent scholars.

sentences.zh: 劉基、宋濂、葉琛、章溢之見聘也，大海實薦之。

translations.literal: When Liu Ji, Song Lian, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi were invited to office, it was Dahai who had truly recommended them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji, Song Lian, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi were invited to serve, it was Dahai who had recommended them.

sentences.zh: 追封越國公，諡武庄，肖像功臣廟，配享太廟。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yue with the posthumous title Wu Zhuang; his portrait was placed in the Temple of Meritorious Ministers and he was granted sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yue with the posthumous title Wu Zhuang (Martial and Dignified); his portrait was placed in the Temple of Meritorious Ministers and he was granted sacrifice in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖克婺州，禁釀酒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founding Emperor took Wuzhou, he forbade the brewing of wine.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor first captured Wuzhou, he banned the brewing of wine.

sentences.zh: 大海子首犯之。

translations.literal: Dahai's son was the first to violate the ban.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai's son was the first to break the ban.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，欲行法。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was angry and wished to carry out the law.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was furious and ordered him punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 時大海方征越，都事王愷請勿誅，以安大海心。

translations.literal: At the time Dahai was campaigning in Yue; Chief Secretary Wang Kai asked that he not be executed, to reassure Dahai's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai was then campaigning in Yue; Chief Secretary Wang Kai pleaded against execution so as not to unsettle Dahai.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「寧可使大海叛我，不可使我法不行。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Better that Dahai rebel against me than that my law not be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor replied: "I would rather have Dahai rebel against me than let the law go unenforced.

sentences.zh: 」竟手刃之。

translations.literal: " In the end he slew him with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he killed the boy with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 及關住復被殺，大海遂無後。

translations.literal: When Guanzhu was later killed as well, Dahai was left without heirs.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhu was later killed as well, Dahai left no heirs.

sentences.zh: 養子 德濟

translations.literal: Adopted son Deji
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son, Deji

sentences.zh: 養子德濟，字世美，不知何許人。

translations.literal: The adopted son Deji, courtesy name Shimei, was a man of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Deji, whose courtesy name was Shimei, was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 大海帥以歸太祖。

translations.literal: Dahai led him back to submit to the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai brought him to join the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 從攻婺州，為誘兵，大破元兵於梅花門外，擒其將季彌章，由是知名。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Wuzhou as decoy troops, greatly defeated Yuan troops outside Meihua Gate, and captured their general Ji Mizhang; from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Wuzhou he served as bait, routed the Yuan army outside Meihua Gate, and captured their general Ji Mizhang, winning fame thereby.

sentences.zh: 既下信州，太祖以德濟為行樞密院同僉，使守之。

translations.literal: After Xinzhou was taken, the Founding Emperor appointed Deji Associate Administrator of the Branch Secretariat and ordered him to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: After Xinzhou fell, the founding emperor appointed Deji associate administrator of the branch secretariat and ordered him to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒將李明道來寇，德濟與力戰。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang's general Li Mingdao came to raid; Deji fought him fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang's general Li Mingdao attacked, Deji fought him fiercely.

sentences.zh: 大海來援，夾擊之，擒明道及其宣慰王漢二。

translations.literal: Dahai came to aid; attacking from both sides they captured Mingdao and his Pacification Commissioner Wang Han'er.
translations.idiomatic: Dahai came to relieve him; in a pincer attack they captured Mingdao and his pacification commissioner Wang Han'er.

sentences.zh: 及大海為蔣英所害，處州降將李祐之亦殺院判耿再成以叛。

translations.literal: When Dahai was killed by Jiang Ying, the surrendered Chuzhou general Li Youzhi also killed Vice Director Geng Zaicheng and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: After Dahai was murdered by Jiang Ying, the surrendered Chuzhou general Li Youzhi killed Vice Director Geng Zaicheng and rebelled as well.

sentences.zh: 張士誠聞浙東亂，遣其弟士信寇諸全。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng, hearing of disorder in eastern Zhe, sent his younger brother Shixin to raid Zhuju.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of disorder in eastern Zhe, Zhang Shicheng sent his younger brother Shixin to attack Zhuju.

sentences.zh: 德濟自信州往救，乘懈得入城，與知州欒鳳、院判謝再興分門守。

translations.literal: Deji went from Xinzhou to relieve the city, entered while the enemy was slack, and with Prefect Luan Feng and Vice Director Xie Zaixing defended the gates separately.
translations.idiomatic: Deji marched from Xinzhou to relieve the city, slipped in while the enemy was off guard, and with Prefect Luan Feng and Vice Director Xie Zaixing held the gates between them.

sentences.zh: 夜半，出敵不意，砍士信營，破走之。

translations.literal: At midnight, taking the enemy unawares, they stormed Shixin's camp and defeated and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they struck Shixin's camp by surprise, routed him, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 擢浙江行省參知政事，移守新城。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat and transferred to guard Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice administrator of the Zhejiang branch secretariat and transferred to guard Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 士誠將李伯升帥步騎大入寇。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng's general Li Bosheng led infantry and cavalry in a major invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng's general Li Bosheng led a large force of infantry and cavalry against him.

sentences.zh: 德濟固守，乞師於李文忠。

translations.literal: Deji held firm and begged troops from Li Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Deji held the city and urgently requested reinforcements from Li Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 文忠馳救，德濟出兵夾擊，大破之，詳文忠傳。

translations.literal: Wenzhong raced to the rescue; Deji sallied forth in a pincer attack and inflicted a great defeat—the details are in Wenzhong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong raced to the rescue; Deji sallied out in a pincer attack and inflicted a crushing defeat, as recounted in Wenzhong's biography.

sentences.zh: 時德濟所部有潛移家入新城者，文忠疑德濟使然。

translations.literal: At the time some of Deji's troops had secretly moved their families into Xincheng; Wenzhong suspected Deji had ordered it.
translations.idiomatic: Some of Deji's men had secretly moved their families into Xincheng; Wenzhong suspected Deji had ordered it.

sentences.zh: 誅其都事羅彥敬，欲微戒德濟。

translations.literal: He executed Deji's Chief Secretary Luo Yanjing, intending a slight warning to Deji.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Deji's chief secretary Luo Yanjing, intending a subtle warning to Deji.

sentences.zh: 將士皆怒，走告德濟。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were all angry and ran to tell Deji.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers were furious and ran to tell Deji.

sentences.zh: 德濟怡然曰：「右丞殺彥敬，自為廣信作戰衣有弊耳，再言者斬！

translations.literal: Deji said calmly: "The Right Chancellor killed Yanjing only because there was a flaw in the battle garments made for Guangxin—speak of it again and you die!
translations.idiomatic: Deji said calmly: "The right chancellor killed Yanjing only because the battle garments made for Guangxin were defective. Anyone who speaks of it again will be executed!

sentences.zh: 」於是太祖召德濟褒諭之，而責文忠失將士心。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Founding Emperor summoned Deji and praised him, while rebuking Wenzhong for losing the hearts of officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " The founding emperor then summoned Deji to praise him and rebuked Wenzhong for losing the loyalty of his troops.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「胡德濟之量，汝不及也。

translations.literal: He also said: "In breadth of mind Hu Deji surpasses you.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Hu Deji's magnanimity is beyond yours.

sentences.zh: 」擢浙江行省右丞，賜駿馬。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat and granted a fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: " Deji was promoted to right chancellor of the Zhejiang branch secretariat and granted a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改左丞，移鎮杭州。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Left Chancellor and transferred to garrison Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made left chancellor and transferred to garrison Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍徐達出定西。

translations.literal: He followed the Grand General Xu Da in the campaign out of Dingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand General Xu Da on the Dingxi campaign.

sentences.zh: 德濟軍失利，達斬其部將數人，械至京師。

translations.literal: Deji's army suffered defeat; Xu Da executed several of his subordinate generals and sent Deji in fetters to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Deji's army suffered defeat, Xu Da executed several of his subordinate generals and sent Deji to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 帝念舊功，釋之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful of old services, released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful of his past service, pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 復以為都指揮使，鎮陝西，卒。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Chief Commander and garrisoned Shaanxi, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed chief commander and garrisoned Shaanxi, where he died.

sentences.zh: 附 樂鳯

translations.literal: Appended: Luan Feng
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Luan Feng

sentences.zh: 欒鳳，高郵人。

translations.literal: Luan Feng, a man of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Luan Feng was a native of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 知諸全，有能聲。

translations.literal: As prefect of Zhuju he had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Zhuju he enjoyed a reputation for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 方士信來攻，與謝再興力守，數出奇兵挫敵。

translations.literal: When Shixin came to attack, he and Xie Zaixing defended resolutely and several times sent surprise troops to check the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shixin attacked, he and Xie Zaixing held the city resolutely and repeatedly sent surprise detachments to blunt the enemy.

sentences.zh: 再興使部校鬻貨於杭，太祖慮其輸我軍虛實，召再興還，而以參軍李夢庚總制諸全軍馬。

translations.literal: Zaixing had his officers sell goods in Hangzhou; the Founding Emperor feared they would reveal our army's strengths and weaknesses, recalled Zaixing, and put Staff Officer Li Menggeng in overall command of Zhuju's forces.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing had his officers trade in Hangzhou; fearing they would reveal military intelligence, the founding emperor recalled Zaixing and placed Staff Officer Li Menggeng in overall command at Zhuju.

sentences.zh: 既而念再興功，為兄子文正娶其長女，命徐達娶其幼女。

translations.literal: Later, mindful of Zaixing's services, he had his elder brother's son Wenzheng marry Zaixing's eldest daughter and ordered Xu Da to marry his younger daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Later, mindful of Zaixing's merit, he had his nephew Wenzheng marry Zaixing's eldest daughter and ordered Xu Da to marry the younger.

sentences.zh: 復遣守諸全。

translations.literal: He was again sent to guard Zhuju.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing was again sent to guard Zhuju.

sentences.zh: 再興忿夢庚出己上，鳳復以細故繩之，遂叛，殺鳳。

translations.literal: Zaixing resented that Menggeng was placed above him; Feng again disciplined him over trifles, so he rebelled and killed Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Zaixing resented Menggeng's authority over him; when Feng disciplined him over a minor matter, he rebelled and killed Feng.

sentences.zh: 鳳妻王氏以身蔽鳳，並殺之。

translations.literal: Feng's wife Lady Wang shielded Feng with her body and was killed together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's wife Lady Wang shielded him with her body and was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 執夢庚，降於士誠，夢庚亦死之。

translations.literal: He seized Menggeng, surrendered to Shicheng, and Menggeng also died.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Menggeng, surrendered to Shicheng, and Menggeng was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖以再興數有功，叛非其志，故鳳與夢庚皆不得恤雲。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, because Zaixing had repeatedly achieved merit and rebellion was not his intent, therefore granted neither Feng nor Menggeng funeral subsidies.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zaixing had served with distinction and the rebellion was not deemed his true intent, neither Feng nor Menggeng received posthumous honors or funeral grants.

sentences.zh: 耿再成

translations.literal: Geng Zaicheng
translations.idiomatic: Geng Zaicheng

sentences.zh: 耿再成，字德甫，五河人。

translations.literal: Geng Zaicheng, courtesy name Defu, a man of Wuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Zaicheng, whose courtesy name was Defu, was a native of Wuhe.

sentences.zh: 從太祖於濠，克泗、滁州。

translations.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor at Hao and captured Si and Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the founding emperor at Hao and helped capture Si and Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元兵圍六合，太祖救之，與再成軍瓦梁壘。

translations.literal: Yuan troops besieged Liuhe; the Founding Emperor went to relieve it and encamped with Zaicheng at Walian.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan forces besieged Liuhe, the founding emperor marched to relieve it and encamped with Zaicheng at Walian.

sentences.zh: 力戰，度不敵，引還。

translations.literal: Fighting fiercely, judging they could not match the enemy, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After fierce fighting, seeing they could not prevail, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元兵尾至，太祖設伏澗側，令再成誘敵，大敗之。

translations.literal: Yuan troops pursued; the Founding Emperor set an ambush beside a ravine and ordered Zaicheng to lure the enemy, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan troops pursued; the founding emperor set an ambush by a ravine and had Zaicheng lure the enemy into a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 以鎮撫從渡江，下集慶。

translations.literal: As Pacification Commissioner he followed in the crossing of the Yangzi and took Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: As pacification commissioner he followed the Yangzi crossing and took Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 以元帥守鎮江，以行樞密院判官守長興，再守揚州。

translations.literal: As marshal he guarded Zhenjiang; as Branch Secretariat Vice Director he guarded Changxing, and again guarded Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as marshal at Zhenjiang, as branch secretariat vice director at Changxing, and again at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 從取金華，為前鋒，屯縉雲之黃龍山以遏敵沖。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Jinhua as vanguard and encamped at Huanglong Mountain in Jinyun to block the enemy's thrust.
translations.idiomatic: In the capture of Jinhua he served as vanguard and encamped at Huanglong Mountain in Jinyun to block the enemy advance.

sentences.zh: 與胡大海破石抹宜孫於處州，克其城，守之。

translations.literal: With Hu Dahai he defeated Shimo Yisun at Chuzhou, took the city, and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: With Hu Dahai he defeated Shimo Yisun at Chuzhou, captured the city, and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 宜孫來攻，又敗之慶元。

translations.literal: When Yisun came to attack, he defeated him again at Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yisun attacked again, he defeated him at Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 再成持軍嚴，士卒出入民間，蔬果無所捐。

translations.literal: Zaicheng held the army strictly; when soldiers passed through villages they took no fruit or vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Zaicheng ran a strict army; when his men passed through villages they took no fruit or vegetables.

sentences.zh: 金華苗帥蔣英等叛，殺胡大海。

translations.literal: The Jinhua Miao commander Jiang Ying and others rebelled and killed Hu Dahai.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinhua tribal commander Jiang Ying and others rebelled and murdered Hu Dahai.

sentences.zh: 處州苗帥李祐之等聞之，亦作亂。

translations.literal: The Chuzhou Miao commanders Li Youzhi and others, hearing of this, also rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the Chuzhou tribal commanders Li Youzhi and others also rebelled.

sentences.zh: 再成方對客飯，聞變，上馬，收戰卒不滿二十人，迎賊罵曰：「賊奴！

translations.literal: Zaicheng was dining with guests when he heard the disturbance; mounting his horse, he gathered fewer than twenty fighting men and met the rebels, cursing: "Rebel scum!
translations.idiomatic: Zaicheng was dining with guests when he heard the alarm. Mounting his horse, he gathered fewer than twenty men and rode out to curse the rebels: "Rebel scum!

sentences.zh: 國家何負汝，乃反。

translations.literal: What has the state done to you that you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: What has the state done to you that you turn traitor.

sentences.zh: 」賊攢槊刺再成。

translations.literal: " The rebels thrust with spears at Zaicheng.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels thrust at Zaicheng with spears.

sentences.zh: 再成揮劍連斷數槊，中傷墜馬，大罵不絕口死。

translations.literal: Zaicheng swung his sword and severed several spears; wounded, he fell from his horse and died cursing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Zaicheng cut down several spears with his sword, was wounded, fell from his horse, and died still cursing.

sentences.zh: 胡深等收其屍，藁葬之。

translations.literal: Hu Shen and others recovered his body and buried it in straw.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shen and others recovered his body and gave it a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 後改葬金陵聚寶山。

translations.literal: Later he was reburied at Treasure-Gathering Mountain in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reburied at Treasure-Gathering Mountain in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 追封高陽郡公，侑享太廟，肖像功臣廟。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang, granted secondary sacrifice in the Grand Temple, and his portrait placed in the Temple of Meritorious Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang, granted secondary sacrifice in the Grand Temple, and his portrait placed in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers.

sentences.zh: 洪武十年加贈泗國公，諡武壯。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongwu he was further granted Duke of Si with the posthumous title Wu Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year ten he was further granted Duke of Si with the posthumous title Wu Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子天璧，聞父難，糾部曲殺賊。

translations.literal: His son Tianbi, hearing of his father's peril, gathered his retainers to kill the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianbi, hearing of his father's death, gathered retainers to avenge him.

sentences.zh: 比至，李文忠已破賊斬之。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Li Wenzhong had already defeated the rebels and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Li Wenzhong had already defeated the rebels and executed them.

sentences.zh: 遂以天璧守處州。

translations.literal: Tianbi was then appointed to guard Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed to hold Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 拒方國珍、張士誠皆有功，擢指揮副使。

translations.literal: In resisting Fang Guozhen and Zhang Shicheng he achieved merit and was promoted to Deputy Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He won merit resisting Fang Guozhen and Zhang Shicheng and was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 克浦城，搗建寧，走陳友定。

translations.literal: He captured Pucheng, raided Jianning, and drove off Chen Youding.
translations.idiomatic: He took Pucheng, raided Jianning, and put Chen Youding to flight.

sentences.zh: 征襄陽，進至西安。

translations.literal: Campaigning at Xiangyang, he advanced as far as Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiangyang campaign he advanced as far as Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 招諭河州、臨洮，皆下。

translations.literal: He induced Hezhou and Lintao to submit; both fell.
translations.idiomatic: He induced Hezhou and Lintao to submit, and both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 改杭州指揮同知。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Associate Commander at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to associate commander at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年出海捕倭，深入外洋，溺死。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he went to sea against the Wo pirates, penetrated deep into the outer ocean, and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he put to sea against Wo pirates, penetrated deep into the open ocean, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 張德勝

translations.literal: Zhang Desheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Desheng

translations.literal: Opening editorial bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Opening editorial bracket marking an appended biography.

sentences.zh: （汪興祖）〉

translations.literal: (Wang Xingzu) closing editorial bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography of Wang Xingzu; closing editorial bracket.

sentences.zh: 張德勝，字仁輔，合肥人。

translations.literal: Zhang Desheng, courtesy name Renfu, a man of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Desheng, whose courtesy name was Renfu, was a native of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 才略雄邁。

translations.literal: His talent and strategy were bold and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: His talent and strategic vision were bold and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 與俞通海等以舟師自巢來歸。

translations.literal: With Yu Tonghai and others he brought a fleet from Chao to submit.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu Tonghai and others he brought a fleet from Chao Lake to submit.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，克採石、太平。

translations.literal: He followed in the crossing of the Yangzi and captured Caishi and Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Yangzi crossing and captured Caishi and Taiping.

sentences.zh: 陳埜先來攻，與湯和等破擒之。

translations.literal: When Chen Yexian came to attack, he with Tang He and others defeated and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yexian attacked, he and Tang He defeated and captured him.

sentences.zh: 授太平興國翼總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director-General of the Taiping Xingguo Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director-general of the Taiping Xingguo wing.

sentences.zh: 破蠻子海牙水寨，擒陳兆先。

translations.literal: He broke Balutu Haiya's river stockade and captured Chen Zhaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Haiya's river stockade and captured Chen Zhaoxian.

sentences.zh: 下集慶，克鎮江，授秦淮翼元帥。

translations.literal: He took Jiqing, captured Zhenjiang, and was appointed Marshal of the Qinhuai Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jiqing, captured Zhenjiang, and was appointed marshal of the Qinhuai wing.

sentences.zh: 取常州，擢樞密院判。

translations.literal: He took Changzhou and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Changzhou and was promoted to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 克寧國，收長槍兵。

translations.literal: He captured Ningguo and recruited long-spear troops.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Ningguo and recruited long-spear troops.

sentences.zh: 下太湖，略馬跡山。

translations.literal: He descended on Lake Tai and raided Maji Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Lake Tai and took Maji Mountain.

sentences.zh: 攻宜興，取馬馱沙及石牌寨。

translations.literal: He attacked Yixing and took Maituosha and the Shibai stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yixing and took Maituosha and the Shibai stockade.

sentences.zh: 進僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Associate Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙普勝陷池州，德勝往援，弗及，還，從徐達拔宜興。

translations.literal: When Zhao Pusheng took Chizhou, Desheng went to relieve it but did not arrive in time; returning, he followed Xu Da in taking Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pusheng seized Chizhou, Desheng went to relieve it but arrived too late; on his return he followed Xu Da in taking Yixing.

sentences.zh: 普勝復掠青陽、石埭。

translations.literal: Pusheng again raided Qingyang and Shidi.
translations.idiomatic: Pusheng again raided Qingyang and Shidi.

sentences.zh: 德勝與戰柵江口，破走之。

translations.literal: Desheng fought him at the stockade on the river mouth and defeated and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng fought him at the river-mouth stockade and routed him.

sentences.zh: 已，復同通海擊敗其眾，遂復池州。

translations.literal: Later, together with Tonghai, he again defeated their host and thus recovered Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Tonghai, he again defeated their forces and recovered Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 引兵自無為趨浮山，走普勝將胡總管，追，敗之青山，逐北至潛山。

translations.literal: Leading troops from Wuwei toward Fushan, he drove off Pusheng's general Hu, pursued, defeated him at Qingshan, and chased him north to Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Marching from Wuwei toward Fushan, he drove off Pusheng's general Hu, pursued him, defeated him at Qingshan, and chased him north to Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒將郭泰逆戰沙河，破斬之，遂克潛山。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang's general Guo Tai met him in battle at Shahe; he was defeated and beheaded, and Qianshan was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's general Guo Tai met him at Shahe; Desheng defeated and beheaded him, then took Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 友諒犯龍江，德勝總舟師迎戰，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: When Youliang raided Longjiang, Desheng commanded the fleet to meet him in battle; casualties were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: When Youliang raided Longjiang, Desheng commanded the fleet; casualties on both sides were heavy.

sentences.zh: 德勝大呼，麾諸將奮擊。

translations.literal: Desheng shouted loudly and waved the generals to strike fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng shouted and urged his generals to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 友諒軍披靡，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Youliang's army collapsed in rout and was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's army broke and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 與諸將追及之慈湖，縱火焚其舟。

translations.literal: Together with other generals he pursued to Cihu and set fire to burn their boats.
translations.idiomatic: With other generals he pursued them to Cihu and burned their fleet.

sentences.zh: 至採石，大戰，沒於陣。

translations.literal: At Caishi they fought a great battle and he perished in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At Caishi they fought a great battle, and he fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 追封蔡國公，諡忠毅，肖像功臣廟，侑享太廟。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Cai with the posthumous title Zhong Yi; his portrait was placed in the Temple of Meritorious Ministers and he was granted secondary sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Cai with the posthumous title Zhong Yi; his portrait was placed in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers and he was granted sacrifice in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 子宣幼。

translations.literal: His son Xuan was young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan was still a child.

sentences.zh: 養子興祖嗣職。
