translations.literal: The adopted son Xingzu succeeded to his office.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Xingzu succeeded to his post.

sentences.zh: 興祖，巢人。

translations.literal: Xingzu was a man of Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu was a native of Chao.

sentences.zh: 本汪姓。

translations.literal: His original surname was Wang.
translations.idiomatic: His original family name was Wang.

sentences.zh: 既嗣職，從破安慶，克江州，拔蘄、黃，取南昌。

translations.literal: After succeeding to the office, he followed in the capture of Anqing, took Jiangzhou, seized Qi and Huang, and captured Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: After succeeding to the post, he helped capture Anqing, took Jiangzhou, seized Qi and Huang, and captured Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 從援安豐，大敗張士誠兵。

translations.literal: He followed in the relief of Anfeng and greatly defeated Zhang Shicheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Anfeng and routed Zhang Shicheng's forces.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽之戰，與廖永忠等以六舟深入。

translations.literal: In the battle at Poyang, with Liao Yongzhong and others he sent six boats deep into the enemy line.
translations.idiomatic: At Poyang he and Liao Yongzhong and others sent six boats deep into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 又邀擊友諒於涇江口。

translations.literal: He also intercepted Youliang at the mouth of the Jing River.
translations.idiomatic: He also intercepted Youliang at the Jing River mouth.

sentences.zh: 功最，擢湖廣行省參政。

translations.literal: His merit was foremost and he was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His merit ranked first, and he was promoted to vice administrator of the Huguang branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從平武昌，遂克廬州，略地至通州而還。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Wuchang, then captured Luzhou, raided as far as Tongzhou, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Wuchang, captured Luzhou, raided as far as Tongzhou, and returned.

sentences.zh: 進大都督府僉事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Associate of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 從徐達取淮東，下浙西。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in taking eastern Huai and reducing western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in taking eastern Huai and reducing western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 進同知大都督府事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Director of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 大軍北征，別將衛軍由徐州克沂、青、東平，乘勝至東阿，降元參政陳璧及所部五萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the great northern campaign, as a separate commander he led troops from Xuzhou to take Yi, Qing, and Dongping, pressed the victory to Dong'e, and induced Yuan Vice Administrator Chen Bi and more than fifty thousand of his troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the northern campaign he led a separate force from Xuzhou through Yi, Qing, and Dongping to Dong'e, where Yuan Vice Administrator Chen Bi and more than fifty thousand troops surrendered.

sentences.zh: 孔子五十六世孫衍聖公希學帥曲阜知縣希舉、鄒縣主簿孟思諒等迎謁於軍門，興祖禮之。

translations.literal: Confucius's fifty-sixth-generation descendant, the Duke of Yansheng Xixue, with Qufu Magistrate Xiju, Zou County Registrar Meng Silang, and others came to pay respects at the army gate; Xingzu received them with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's fifty-sixth-generation descendant, Duke of Yansheng Xixue, with Qufu Magistrate Xiju and others came to pay respects at the army gate, and Xingzu received them with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 兗東州縣聞風皆下，遂取濟寧、濟南。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties of eastern Yan all submitted on hearing the news; he then took Jining and Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yan prefectures and counties submitted on hearing the news, and he took Jining and Jinan.

sentences.zh: 興祖子幼，命與宣同居。

translations.literal: Xingzu's son was young; he was ordered to live together with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xingzu's son was young, he was ordered to live with Xuan.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，爵除。

translations.literal: He died of illness and the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness, and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 趙德勝

translations.literal: Zhao Desheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Desheng

sentences.zh: 趙德勝，濠人。

translations.literal: Zhao Desheng, a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Desheng was a native of Hao.

sentences.zh: 為元義兵長，善馬槊，每戰先登。

translations.literal: He was a Yuan righteous-army commander, skilled with the horse lance, and in every battle was first over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a Yuan righteous-army commander, skilled with the cavalry lance, and was always first in the assault.

sentences.zh: 隸王忙哥麾下，察其必敗。

translations.literal: He served under Wang Mangge and perceived that he was doomed to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Wang Mangge but saw that defeat was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 太祖取滁陽，德勝母在軍中，乃棄其妻來從。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took Chuyang, Desheng's mother was in the army; he abandoned his wife and came to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took Chuyang, Desheng's mother was in Mangge's army; he abandoned his wife and joined the founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，賜之名，為帳前先鋒。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was pleased, bestowed a name on him, and made him vanguard before the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was pleased, gave him the name Desheng, and made him vanguard of the headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 從取鐵佛岡，攻三汊河，破張家寨，克全椒、後河諸寨。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Tiefogang, attacked San Cha River, broke Zhang Family Stockade, and captured Quanjiao and Houhe stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He took Tiefogang, attacked San Cha River, broke Zhang Family Stockade, and captured Quanjiao and the Houhe stockades.

sentences.zh: 援六合，中流矢，幾殆。

translations.literal: Relieving Liuhe, he was struck by an arrow midstream and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: At Liuhe he was struck by an arrow and nearly died.

sentences.zh: 擊雞籠山，搗烏江，下和州、含山。

translations.literal: He struck Jilong Mountain, raided Wujiang, and reduced Hezhou and Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Jilong Mountain, raided Wujiang, and took Hezhou and Hanshan.

sentences.zh: 夜襲陳埜先營，拔板門、鐵長官二寨，遂取儀真。

translations.literal: By night he raided Chen Yexian's camp, took Banmen and Tie Zhangguan stockades, and thus captured Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: In a night attack on Chen Yexian's camp he took Banmen and Tie Zhangguan stockades and captured Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 授總管府先鋒。

translations.literal: He was appointed vanguard of the Directorate-General.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vanguard of the directorate-general.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，下太平，克蕪湖、句容、溧水、溧陽，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed in the crossing of the Yangzi, took Taiping, and captured Wuhu, Jurong, Lishui, and Liyang, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi, took Taiping, and captured Wuhu, Jurong, Lishui, and Liyang with distinction.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春敗蠻子海牙於採石，破陳兆先營於方山，下集慶，功最。

translations.literal: He followed Chang Yuchun in defeating Balutu Haiya at Caishi, breaking Chen Zhaoxian's camp at Fangshan, and taking Jiqing; his merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: With Chang Yuchun he defeated Haiya at Caishi, broke Chen Zhaoxian's camp at Fangshan, and took Jiqing, winning the highest merit.

sentences.zh: 從徐達取鎮江，破苗軍水寨。

translations.literal: He followed Xu Da in taking Zhenjiang and broke the Miao army's river stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da in taking Zhenjiang and broke the tribal army's river stockade.

sentences.zh: 下丹陽、金壇，平寧國。

translations.literal: He reduced Danyang and Jintan and pacified Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: He took Danyang and Jintan and pacified Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 轉領軍先鋒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to army vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to army vanguard.

sentences.zh: 取廣德，破張士誠水寨。

translations.literal: He took Guangde and broke Zhang Shicheng's river stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Guangde and broke Zhang Shicheng's river stockade.

sentences.zh: 復從遇春攻常州，解牛塘圍，復廣德、寧國。

translations.literal: Again he followed Yuchun in attacking Changzhou, relieved the siege at Niutang, and recovered Guangde and Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Again with Yuchun he attacked Changzhou, relieved the siege at Niutang, and recovered Guangde and Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 取江陰，攻常熟，擒張士德。

translations.literal: He took Jiangyin, attacked Changshu, and captured Zhang Shide.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jiangyin, attacked Changshu, and captured Zhang Shide.

sentences.zh: 從攻湖州。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the attack on Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 宜興叛，還兵定之。

translations.literal: Yixing rebelled; he returned and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixing rebelled, he returned and pacified it.

sentences.zh: 擢中翼左副元帥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Marshal of the Central Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice marshal of the central wing.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒犯龍江。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang raided Longjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang raided Longjiang.

sentences.zh: 龍江第一關曰虎口城，太祖以屬德勝。

translations.literal: The first pass at Longjiang was called Tiger Mouth City; the Founding Emperor entrusted it to Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: The first pass at Longjiang was Tiger Mouth City; the founding emperor entrusted it to Desheng.

sentences.zh: 友諒至，力戰。

translations.literal: When Youliang arrived, Desheng fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: When Youliang arrived, Desheng fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 伏兵起，友諒大敗。

translations.literal: Ambush troops rose and Youliang was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ambush troops rose and Youliang suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 遂復太平。

translations.literal: Taiping was thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping was then recovered.

sentences.zh: 下銅陵臨山寨，略黃山橋及馬馱沙，征高郵。

translations.literal: He reduced Tongling Linshan stockade, raided Huangshan Bridge and Maituosha, and campaigned at Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: He took Tongling's Linshan stockade, raided Huangshan Bridge and Maituosha, and campaigned at Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 有功，進後翼統軍元帥。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Marshal of the Rear Wing Command.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to marshal of the rear wing command.

sentences.zh: 從太祖西征，破安慶水寨，乘風溯小孤山。

translations.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor on the western campaign, broke Anqing's river stockade, and rode the wind up past Little Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the western campaign, broke Anqing's river stockade, and sailed up past Little Gushan with the wind.

sentences.zh: 距九江五里，友諒始知，倉皇遁去。

translations.literal: Five li from Jiujiang, Youliang only then learned of it and fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Five li from Jiujiang, Youliang only then learned of the approach and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 遂克九江，徇黃梅、廣濟，克瑞昌、臨江、吉安，還下安慶。

translations.literal: Jiujiang was thus taken; he swept Huangmei and Guangji, captured Ruichang, Linjiang, and Ji'an, and returned to reduce Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jiujiang, swept Huangmei and Guangji, captured Ruichang, Linjiang, and Ji'an, and returned to take Anqing.

sentences.zh: 進克撫州，取新淦。

translations.literal: Advancing, he captured Fuzhou and took Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to capture Fuzhou and took Xingan.

sentences.zh: 討南昌叛將，復其城，砲傷肩。

translations.literal: He suppressed the rebel generals at Nanchang, recovered the city, and was wounded in the shoulder by cannon fire.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed Nanchang's rebel generals, recovered the city, and was wounded in the shoulder by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 授僉江南行樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Associate of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate of the Jiangnan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與硃文正、鄧愈共守南昌。

translations.literal: Together with Zhu Wenzheng and Deng Yu he jointly defended Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhu Wenzheng and Deng Yu he defended Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 平羅友賢於池州，破友諒將於西山。

translations.literal: He pacified Luo Youxian at Chizhou and defeated Youliang's generals at Xishan.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Luo Youxian at Chizhou and defeated Youliang's generals at Xishan.

sentences.zh: 復臨江、吉安、撫州。

translations.literal: He recovered Linjiang, Ji'an, and Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Linjiang, Ji'an, and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，友諒大舉兵圍南昌。

translations.literal: Before long Youliang raised a great army to besiege Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Youliang raised a great army to besiege Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 德勝帥所部數千，背城逆戰，射殺其將，敵大沮。

translations.literal: Desheng led several thousand of his troops to fight with their backs to the wall, shot and killed an enemy general, and the enemy was greatly discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng led several thousand men in a desperate fight with their backs to the wall, killed an enemy general with an arrow, and the enemy's morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 明日復合，環城數匝。

translations.literal: The next day they joined battle again and surrounded the city several circuits deep.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the enemy returned and ringed the city several times over.

sentences.zh: 友諒親督戰，晝夜攻，城且壞。

translations.literal: Youliang personally directed the battle; day and night they attacked and the walls were near collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang directed the assault in person; the attacks continued day and night until the walls nearly gave way.

sentences.zh: 德勝帥諸將死戰，且戰且築，城壞復完。

translations.literal: Desheng led the generals in fighting to the death, fighting while building; when the walls broke they were repaired again.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng led the generals in fighting to the death, repairing the walls even as they fought until broken sections were made whole again.

sentences.zh: 暮坐城門樓，指揮士卒。

translations.literal: At dusk he sat on the gate tower directing the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he sat on the gate tower directing the troops.

sentences.zh: 弩中腰膂，鏃入六寸，拔出之，嘆曰：「吾自壯歲從軍，傷矢石屢矣，無重此者。

translations.literal: A crossbow bolt struck his loins; the head entered six inches; pulling it out he sighed: "Since my vigorous years I have followed the army and been wounded by arrows and stones many times, but never as grave as this.
translations.idiomatic: A crossbow bolt struck his loins, the head sinking six inches deep. Pulling it out, he sighed: "Since my vigorous years I have followed the army and been wounded many times, but never as gravely as this.

sentences.zh: 丈夫死不恨，恨不能掃清中原耳。

translations.literal: A man does not regret death, but regrets that he could not sweep clear the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: A man does not regret death, only that he could not sweep the Central Plain clear of enemies.

sentences.zh: 」言畢而絕，年三十九。

translations.literal: " Having spoken, he died, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Having spoken, he died, aged thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 追封梁國公，諡武桓，列祀功臣廟，配享太廟。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Liang with the posthumous title Wu Huan, enshrined in the Temple of Meritorious Ministers, and granted sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Liang with the posthumous title Wu Huan, enshrined in the Hall of Meritorious Ministers, and granted sacrifice in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 德勝剛直沉鷙，馭下嚴肅。

translations.literal: Desheng was upright, stern, and deep; in commanding subordinates he was strict.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng was upright, stern, and reserved; he commanded his subordinates with strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 未嘗讀書，臨機應變，動合古法。

translations.literal: He had never studied books, yet in responding to circumstances on the battlefield his movements accorded with ancient methods.
translations.idiomatic: Though he never studied books, in battle his responses accorded with the principles of classical warfare.

sentences.zh: 平居篤孝友如修士。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was devoted in filial piety and friendship like a cultivated gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he was as devoted in filial piety and friendship as a cultivated gentleman.

sentences.zh: 友諒圍南昌八十五日，先後戰死者凡十四人。

translations.literal: Youliang besieged Nanchang for eighty-five days; in all fourteen men died in battle before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang besieged Nanchang for eighty-five days; fourteen defenders died in battle during the siege.

sentences.zh: 張子明者，領兵千戶也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ziming was a commander of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ziming was a commander of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 洪都圍久，內外隔絕，硃文正遣子明告急於應天。

translations.literal: The siege of Hongdu had lasted long and inside and outside were cut off; Zhu Wenzheng sent Ziming to report the emergency at Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongdu siege had cut the city off from the outside world; Zhu Wenzheng sent Ziming to report the emergency at Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 以東湖小漁舟從水關潛出，夜行晝止，半月始得達。

translations.literal: In a small fishing boat on the eastern lake he slipped out through the water gate, traveling by night and resting by day; in half a month he reached his destination.
translations.idiomatic: In a small fishing boat from the eastern lake he slipped out through the water gate, traveling by night and resting by day, and reached Yingtian in half a month.

sentences.zh: 太祖問友諒兵勢。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor asked about Youliang's military strength.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor asked about Youliang's military strength.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「兵雖盛，戰鬥死者不少。

translations.literal: He replied: "Though their army is large, many have died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Though their army is large, many have already died in battle.

sentences.zh: 今江水日涸，賊巨艦將不利。

translations.literal: Now the river water daily falls; their great ships will be at a disadvantage.
translations.idiomatic: The river is falling daily; their great ships will soon be at a disadvantage.

sentences.zh: 援至可破也。

translations.literal: When relief arrives they can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: When relief arrives they can be defeated.

sentences.zh: 」太祖謂子明：「歸語而帥：堅守一月，吾自取之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor told Ziming: "Return and tell your commander: hold firm one month and I will take them myself.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor told Ziming: "Return and tell your commander to hold for one month; I will come myself.

sentences.zh: 」還至湖口，為友諒所獲。

translations.literal: Returning to Hukou, he was captured by Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Hukou he was captured by Youliang.

sentences.zh: 令誘城中降，子明佯諾。

translations.literal: Youliang ordered him to induce the city to surrender; Ziming pretended to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang ordered him to induce the city to surrender; Ziming pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 至城下，大呼：「我張大舍。

translations.literal: At the foot of the wall he shouted loudly: "I am Zhang the Elder.
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of the wall he shouted: "I am Zhang the Elder!

sentences.zh: 已見主上，令諸公堅守，救且至！

translations.literal: I have seen the sovereign; all of you hold firm—relief is coming soon!
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the sovereign! Hold firm—all of you—relief is coming soon!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，攢槊殺之。

translations.literal: The rebels were enraged and thrust with spears and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was enraged and killed him with spears.

sentences.zh: 追封忠節侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Loyal Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Loyal Integrity.

sentences.zh: 友諒攻撫州，樞密院判李繼先乘城戰死；

translations.literal: Youliang attacked Fuzhou; Branch Secretariat Vice Director Li Jixian died fighting on the wall;
translations.idiomatic: Youliang attacked Fuzhou; Branch Secretariat Vice Director Li Jixian died fighting on the walls;

sentences.zh: 左翼元帥牛海龍突圍死；

translations.literal: Left Wing Marshal Niu Hailong died breaking out of encirclement;
translations.idiomatic: Left Wing Marshal Niu Hailong died breaking out of the encirclement;

sentences.zh: 左副元帥趙國旺引兵燒戰艦，敵追至，投橋下死；

translations.literal: Left Vice Marshal Zhao Guowang led troops to burn the warships; the enemy pursued to the bridge and he threw himself below and died;
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Marshal Zhao Guowang burned the warships; pursued to a bridge, he threw himself into the water and died;

sentences.zh: 百戶徐明躍馬出射賊，賊知明名，並力攻，被執死；

translations.literal: Commander of a Hundred Households Xu Ming leaped out on horseback to shoot the enemy; knowing Ming's name, they attacked together and he was captured and killed;
translations.idiomatic: Commander Xu Ming rode out to shoot at the enemy; recognizing him, they concentrated their attack and captured and killed him;

sentences.zh: 軍士張德山夜半潛出城，焚賊舟，賊覺，死；

translations.literal: Soldier Zhang Deshan slipped out of the city at midnight to burn the enemy boats; the enemy noticed and he died;
translations.idiomatic: Soldier Zhang Deshan slipped out at midnight to burn enemy boats; discovered, he was killed;

sentences.zh: 夏茂成守城樓，中飛砲死；

translations.literal: Xia Maocheng guarded the gate tower and was killed by a flying projectile;
translations.idiomatic: Xia Maocheng guarded a gate tower and was killed by a projectile;

sentences.zh: 右翼元帥同知硃潛、統軍元帥許珪俱戰死。

translations.literal: Right Wing Vice Director Zhu Qian and Marshal Xu Gui both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Right Wing Vice Director Zhu Qian and Marshal Xu Gui both died in battle.

sentences.zh: 蔣必勝陷吉安，參政劉齊、知府硃文華被執，不屈死。

translations.literal: Jiang Bisheng took Ji'an; Vice Administrator Liu Qi and Prefect Zhu Wenhua were captured and died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bisheng took Ji'an; Vice Administrator Liu Qi and Prefect Zhu Wenhua were captured and died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 趙天麟守臨江，友諒攻之，城陷，不屈死。

translations.literal: Zhao Tianlin defended Linjiang; when Youliang attacked and the city fell, he died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tianlin defended Linjiang; when the city fell he died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 祝宗、康泰叛，陷洪都，知府葉琛與行省都事萬思誠迎戰，皆死。

translations.literal: Zhu Zong and Kang Tai rebelled, took Hongdu; Prefect Ye Chen and Branch Secretariat Director Wan Sicheng went out to fight and both died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zong and Kang Tai rebelled and took Hongdu; Prefect Ye Chen and Secretariat Director Wan Sicheng went out to fight and both died.

sentences.zh: 事平，皆贈爵侯伯以下有差，立忠臣廟於豫章，並祠十四人，以德勝為首。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, all were granted posthumous ranks from marquis and earl downward in varying degrees; a Temple of Loyal Ministers was established at Yuzhang, enshrining the fourteen with Desheng foremost.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, all received posthumous ranks; a Temple of Loyal Ministers was built at Yuzhang enshrining the fourteen, with Desheng foremost.

sentences.zh: 而康郎山戰死者三十五人，首丁普郎。

translations.literal: At Kanglang Mountain thirty-five men died in battle, led by Ding Pulang.
translations.idiomatic: At Kanglang Mountain thirty-five men died in battle, Ding Pulang foremost among them.

sentences.zh: 普郎初為陳友諒將，守小孤山。

translations.literal: At first Pu Lang was a general of Chen Youliang, guarding Little Solitary Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Lang had originally served Chen Youliang as a general, holding Little Solitary Mountain.

sentences.zh: 偕傅友德來降，授行樞密院同知，數有功。

translations.literal: He came to submit together with Fu Youde, was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Mobile Privy Council, and achieved merit many times.
translations.idiomatic: He defected together with Fu Youde, was made vice commissioner of the mobile privy council, and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 及援南昌，大戰鄱陽湖。

translations.literal: When they went to relieve Nanchang, a great battle was fought on Poyang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched to relieve Nanchang, they fought a great battle on Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 自辰至午，普郎身被十余創，首脫猶直立，執兵作斗狀，敵驚為神。

translations.literal: From the hour chen to the hour wu, Pu Lang received more than ten wounds on his body; his head was severed yet he still stood upright, holding his weapon in a fighting posture, and the enemy were awed, taking him for a god.
translations.idiomatic: From morning until midday Pu Lang took more than a dozen wounds; even after his head was struck off he remained standing, weapon raised as if still fighting, and the enemy took him for a supernatural being.

sentences.zh: 時七月己丑也。

translations.literal: The time was the day jichou of the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: This took place on the jichou day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 追贈濟陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 張志雄亦友諒將，素驍勇，號長張。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhixiong was also a general of Youliang, by nature fierce and brave, and was called Long Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhixiong, another of Youliang's generals, was famed for valor and known as "Long Zhang."

sentences.zh: 從趙普勝守安慶。

translations.literal: He followed Zhao Pusheng in guarding Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: He had followed Zhao Pusheng in the defense of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 友諒殺普勝，志雄怨，來降，為樞密院判。

translations.literal: Youliang killed Pusheng; Zhixiong bore a grudge, came to submit, and was made a judge of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: When Youliang killed Pusheng, Zhixiong, resentful, defected and was appointed a privy council judge.

sentences.zh: 至是舟檣折，敵攢刺之，知不能脫，遂自刎。

translations.literal: On this occasion his mast and oars were broken; the enemy thrust at him in a crowd; knowing he could not escape, he cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: In the battle his ship was crippled and the enemy closed in with spears; seeing no escape, he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 元帥余昶、右元帥陳弼、徐公輔皆以其日戰沒。

translations.literal: The marshals Yu Chang, the Right Marshal Chen Bi, and Xu Gongfu all died in battle on that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Marshals Yu Chang, Chen Bi on the right, and Xu Gongfu all fell in battle that same day.

sentences.zh: 先一日，左副指揮韓成，元帥宋貴、陳兆先戰沒。

translations.literal: On the previous day, the Left Vice Commander Han Cheng and the marshals Song Gui and Chen Zhaoxian died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, Left Vice Commander Han Cheng and marshals Song Gui and Chen Zhaoxian had been killed in action.

sentences.zh: 兆先者，埜先從子，既被擒，太祖以其兵備宿衛。

translations.literal: Zhaoxian was a nephew of Chen Yexian; once captured, the Founding Emperor used his troops to strengthen the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxian was Chen Yexian's nephew; after his capture the founding emperor enrolled his men in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 感帝大度，效死力，至是戰死。

translations.literal: Moved by the emperor's magnanimity, he exerted himself unto death; on this occasion he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for the emperor's generosity, he fought to the utmost and now fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 韓成子觀至都督，別有傳。

translations.literal: Han Cheng's son Guan rose to be a regional commander; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Han Cheng's son Guan eventually became a regional commander and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 越四日，辛卯，復大戰，副元帥昌文貴、左元帥李信、王勝、劉義死。

translations.literal: Four days later, on the day xinmao, they fought again in a great battle; the Vice Marshal Chang Wengui, the Left Marshal Li Xin, Wang Sheng, and Liu Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later, on xinmao, another great battle was fought; Vice Marshal Chang Wengui, Left Marshal Li Xin, Wang Sheng, and Liu Yi were killed.

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，扼敵涇江口，同知元帥李志高、副使王咬住亦戰死。

translations.literal: On the day renxu of the eighth month they blocked the enemy at the mouth of the Jing River; the Associate Commander-in-Chief Li Zhigao and the Vice Commissioner Wang Yaozhu also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu of the eighth month the army held the enemy at the Jing River estuary; Associate Commander Li Zhigao and Vice Commissioner Wang Yaozhu also fell.

sentences.zh: 其他偏裨死事者，千戶姜潤、王鳳顯、石明、王德、硃鼎、王清、常德勝、袁華、陳沖、王喜仙、汪澤、丁宇、史德勝、裴軫、王理、王仁，鎮撫常惟德、鄭興、逯德山、羅世榮、曹信。

translations.literal: Among other subordinate officers who died in service were the chiliarchs Jiang Run, Wang Fengxian, Shi Ming, Wang De, Zhu Ding, Wang Qing, Chang Desheng, Yuan Hua, Chen Chong, Wang Xixian, Wang Ze, Ding Yu, Shi Desheng, Pei Zhen, Wang Li, and Wang Ren, and the garrison commissioners Chang Weide, Zheng Xing, Lu Deshan, Luo Shirong, and Cao Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Other officers who died in the line of duty included chiliarchs Jiang Run, Wang Fengxian, Shi Ming, Wang De, Zhu Ding, Wang Qing, Chang Desheng, Yuan Hua, Chen Chong, Wang Xixian, Wang Ze, Ding Yu, Shi Desheng, Pei Zhen, Wang Li, and Wang Ren, and garrison commissioners Chang Weide, Zheng Xing, Lu Deshan, Luo Shirong, and Cao Xin.

sentences.zh: 凡贈公一人、侯十二人、伯二人、子十五人、男六人，肖像康郎山忠臣廟，有司歲致祭。

translations.literal: In all, one was enfeoffed posthumously as duke, twelve as marquis, two as earl, fifteen as viscount, and six as baron; their portraits were placed in the Loyal Ministers Shrine on Kanglang Mountain, and the authorities offered sacrifice each year.
translations.idiomatic: In all one man was posthumously made duke, twelve marquises, two earls, fifteen viscounts, and six barons; their images were installed in the Loyal Ministers Shrine on Kanglang Mountain, with annual sacrifices performed by the officials.

sentences.zh: 又程國勝者，徽人。

translations.literal: There was also Cheng Guosheng, a man of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Cheng Guosheng, from Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 以義兵元帥來歸，敗楊完者。

translations.literal: He came to submit as a righteous-army marshal, and defeated Yang Wanzhe.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted as commander of a volunteer force and defeated Yang Wanzhe.

sentences.zh: 累功至萬戶。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he rose to the rank of chiliarch of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: By repeated merit he rose to the rank of chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 守南昌。

translations.literal: He guarded Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was stationed at Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 與牛海龍夜劫友諒營。

translations.literal: Together with Niu Hailong he raided Youliang's camp by night.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Niu Hailong in a night raid on Youliang's camp.

sentences.zh: 海龍中流矢死，國勝泅水得脫，抵金陵。

translations.literal: Hailong was struck by a flying arrow and died; Guosheng swam away and escaped, reaching Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Hailong was killed by an arrow in flight; Guosheng swam free and made his way to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 從太祖戰鄱陽。

translations.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor in the battle on Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the founding emperor to the battle on Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 張定邊直前犯太祖舟，國勝與韓成、陳兆先駕舸左右奮擊，太祖舟脫。

translations.literal: Zhang Dingbian drove straight forward and attacked the Founding Emperor's boat; Guosheng, together with Han Cheng and Chen Zhaoxian, manned small craft and struck fiercely on either side, and the Founding Emperor's boat escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dingbian bore down on the founding emperor's vessel, Guosheng with Han Cheng and Chen Zhaoxian rowed out in light boats and fought fiercely on both flanks until the emperor's ship broke free.

sentences.zh: 國勝等繞出敵艦後，援絕，力戰死。

translations.literal: Guosheng and the others circled behind the enemy ships; reinforcements were cut off, and they fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Guosheng and his companions circled behind the enemy fleet; cut off from support, they fought until they were killed.

sentences.zh: 而南昌城中謂國勝已前死，故豫章、康山兩廟俱得預祀雲。

translations.literal: Yet within Nanchang city it was thought that Guosheng had already died earlier, and so in both the Yuzhang and Kangshan shrines he was included in advance among those worshipped—thus it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Nanchang had believed Guosheng already dead, so he was honored in advance at both the Yuzhang and Kangshan shrines—hence the remark.

sentences.zh: 桑世傑

translations.literal: Sang Shijie
translations.idiomatic: Sang Shijie

sentences.zh: 桑世傑，無為人。

translations.literal: Sang Shijie was a man of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Shijie was a native of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 亦自巢湖來歸。

translations.literal: He too came to submit from Chaohu Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He too had come over from Chaohu Lake.

sentences.zh: 趙普勝有異志，世傑發其謀，普勝逸去。

translations.literal: Zhao Pusheng harbored a divergent design; Shijie exposed his plot, and Pusheng fled away.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pusheng plotted treason, Shijie exposed him and Pusheng fled.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，以舟師破元水軍。

translations.literal: Following the crossing of the Yangzi, with the fleet he broke the Yuan river forces.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yangzi crossing he shattered the Yuan navy with his fleet.

sentences.zh: 授秦淮翼元帥。

translations.literal: He was appointed marshal of the Qinhuai Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made marshal of the Qinhuai wing.

sentences.zh: 下鎮江，徇金壇、丹陽，攻寧國長槍諸軍，克水陽，平常州。

translations.literal: He took Zhenjiang, swept Jintan and Danyang, attacked the Long-Spear armies of Ningguo, captured Shuiyang, and pacified Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Zhenjiang, overran Jintan and Danyang, attacked the long-spear forces at Ningguo, took Shuiyang, and pacified Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 判行樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was made acting judge of the Mobile Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting judge of the mobile privy council.

sentences.zh: 略地江陰、宜興。

translations.literal: He seized territory in Jiangyin and Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He extended operations into Jiangyin and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 初，石牌民硃定，販鹽無賴，與富民趙氏有隙，遂告變，滅趙氏，授江陰判官。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhu Ding of Shipai, a salt-smuggling ruffian, had a feud with the wealthy Zhao family; he therefore reported them for treason, destroyed the Zhao clan, and was appointed magistrate of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu Ding of Shipai, a salt-smuggling rogue at odds with the wealthy Zhao family, had denounced them for treason, wiped out the clan, and been made magistrate of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 尋復為盜，元遣兵捕之。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to banditry, and the Yuan sent troops to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he turned bandit again, and the Yuan dispatched troops against him.

sentences.zh: 定聞張士誠據高郵，乃導士誠由通州渡江，遂陷平江。

translations.literal: Ding heard that Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou; he therefore guided Shicheng across the river from Tongzhou, and they thereupon took Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou, Ding guided him across from Tongzhou, and together they seized Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 以定為參政，而遣元帥欒瑞戍石牌。

translations.literal: Ding was made a provincial administrator, while Marshal Luan Rui was sent to garrison Shipai.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was made provincial administrator and Marshal Luan Rui was stationed at Shipai.

sentences.zh: 及大兵既取江陰，瑞尚據石牌，導舟師往來。

translations.literal: When the great army had already taken Jiangyin, Rui still held Shipai and guided the fleet back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: After the main forces took Jiangyin, Rui still held Shipai and kept the river route open.

sentences.zh: 太祖命永安及世傑擊之，世傑力戰死，瑞亦降。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered Yongan and Shijie to attack him; Shijie fought fiercely and died, and Rui also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor ordered Yongan and Shijie to strike him; Shijie fell in fierce fighting, and Rui then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 張氏窺江路絕。

translations.literal: The Zhang clan saw that the river route was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng found his river line severed.

sentences.zh: 太祖念其功，贈安遠大將軍、輕車都尉、永義侯，侑享太廟。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, mindful of his merit, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand General of Pacifying the Distant, Commandant of Light Chariots, and Marquis of Everlasting Righteousness, with attendant sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his service, the founding emperor posthumously made him Grand General of Pacifying the Distant, Commandant of Light Chariots, and Marquis of Everlasting Righteousness, with a place in the ancestral temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 子敬以父死事，累官都督府僉事。

translations.literal: His son Jing, because of his father's death in service, rose through offices to be a commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, on account of his father's death in battle, rose to commissioner of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十三年，封徽先伯，歲祿千七百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Earl of Huixian with an annual stipend of seventeen hundred piculs of grain and a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 23 he was enfeoffed as Earl of Huixian, with seventeen hundred piculs yearly and a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 明年同徐輝祖等防邊，尋令屯軍平陽，坐藍玉黨死。

translations.literal: The next year, together with Xu Huizu and others, he guarded the frontier; soon he was ordered to station troops at Pingyang, and was put to death as a member of Lan Yu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Xu Huizu on frontier defense, then was ordered to garrison Pingyang; he was later executed as an associate of Lan Yu's faction.

sentences.zh: 附 劉成

translations.literal: Appendix: Liu Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Liu Cheng

sentences.zh: 又劉成者，靈璧人。

translations.literal: There was also Liu Cheng, a man of Lingbi.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Liu Cheng, from Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 以統兵總管從耿炳文定長興，為永興翼左副元帥，數佐炳文敗士誠兵。

translations.literal: As commander-in-chief of troops he followed Geng Bingwen in pacifying Changxing, became left vice marshal of the Yongxing Wing, and many times assisted Bingwen in defeating Shicheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: As troop commander-in-chief he followed Geng Bingwen in securing Changxing, became left vice marshal of the Yongxing wing, and repeatedly helped defeat Zhang Shicheng's forces.

sentences.zh: 李伯升以十萬眾來攻，城中兵僅七千。

translations.literal: Li Bosheng came to attack with a hundred thousand men; the troops in the city numbered only seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bosheng attacked with one hundred thousand men while the garrison held only seven thousand.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣兵援之，未至，炳文嬰城守。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor sent troops to relieve them; before they arrived, Bingwen shut the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor sent relief, but before it arrived Bingwen closed the walls and defended.

sentences.zh: 成引數士騎出西門，擊敗伯升兵，擒其將宋元帥。

translations.literal: Cheng led several dozen horsemen out the west gate, defeated Bosheng's troops, and captured his general Song Yuanshuai.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng led a few dozen horsemen out the west gate, routed Bosheng's army, and captured his general Song Yuanshuai.

sentences.zh: 轉至東門，敵悉兵圍之，遂戰死。

translations.literal: He then turned to the east gate; the enemy massed all their troops and surrounded him, and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Moving to the east gate he was surrounded by the enemy's full strength and killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈懷遠將軍，立廟長興。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General of Cherishing the Distant, and a temple was erected to him at Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of Cherishing the Distant, with a shrine raised at Changxing.

sentences.zh: 茅成，定遠人。

translations.literal: Mao Cheng was a man of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Cheng was a native of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 自和州從軍，隸常遇春麾下。

translations.literal: From Hezhou he joined the army and served under Chang Yuchun.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service from Hezhou and served under Chang Yuchun.

sentences.zh: 克太平，始授萬戶。

translations.literal: When Taiping was taken, he was first appointed chiliarch of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After the capture of Taiping he was first made chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 從定常州、寧國，進總管。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Changzhou and Ningguo and was promoted to commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Changzhou and Ningguo and was promoted to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 克衢州，授副元帥。

translations.literal: When Quzhou was taken, he was appointed vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On the capture of Quzhou he was made vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 守金華，改太平興國翼元帥。

translations.literal: He guarded Jinhua and was changed to marshal of the Taiping Xingguo Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He held Jinhua and was transferred to marshal of the Taiping Xingguo wing.

sentences.zh: 從克安慶，援安豐，戰鄱陽，克武昌，授武德衛千戶。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Anqing, the relief of Anfeng, the battle on Poyang, and the taking of Wuchang, and was appointed chiliarch of the Wude Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Anqing, relieved Anfeng, battled on Poyang, and took Wuchang, and was appointed chiliarch of the Wude Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋進指揮副使。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 取贛州、安陸、襄陽、泰州，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the seizure of Ganzhou, Anlu, Xiangyang, and Taizhou he had merit each time.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the captures of Ganzhou, Anlu, Xiangyang, and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 從徐達攻平江，焚張士誠戰船，築長圍困之。

translations.literal: Following Xu Da in the attack on Pingjiang, he burned Zhang Shicheng's warships and built a long encirclement to hem him in.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xu Da at Pingjiang he burned Zhang Shicheng's fleet and threw up a long siege line.

sentences.zh: 達攻婁門，士誠出兵戰，成擊敗之。

translations.literal: Da attacked the Lou Gate; Shicheng sent troops out to fight, and Cheng defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da assaulted the Lou Gate, Shicheng sallied forth and Cheng drove him back.

sentences.zh: 突至外郛，中叉死。

translations.literal: He burst through to the outer wall and was killed by a forked weapon.
translations.idiomatic: He charged to the outer ramparts and was killed by a trident.

sentences.zh: 贈東海郡公，祀功臣廟。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Donghai Commandery and worshipped in the Shrine of Meritorious Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Donghai and honored in the Shrine of Meritorious Ministers.

sentences.zh: 附 楊國興

translations.literal: Appendix: Yang Guoxing
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Yang Guoxing

sentences.zh: 同時死者，有楊國興，亦定遠人。

translations.literal: Among those who died at the same time was Yang Guoxing, also a man of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Among those killed in the same fighting was Yang Guoxing, likewise from Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以右翼元帥守宜興。

translations.literal: As right-wing marshal he guarded Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: As right-wing marshal he held Yixing.

sentences.zh: 初，常州人陳保二聚眾，號「黃包軍」。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chen Baoer of Changzhou had gathered a crowd and called themselves the "Yellow-Cloth Army."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chen Baoer of Changzhou had raised a band known as the "Yellow-Cloth Army."

sentences.zh: 即降復叛，誘執詹、李二將。

translations.literal: Having submitted, he rebelled again and lured and seized the two generals Zhan and Li.
translations.idiomatic: He had submitted, then rebelled again, and by treachery seized Generals Zhan and Li.

sentences.zh: 國興執斬之。

translations.literal: Guoxing seized and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxing captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 授神武衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of the Shenwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the Shenwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 至是攻閶門戰死，以其子益襲指揮使。

translations.literal: On this occasion he died in battle attacking the Chang Gate; his son Yi inherited the post of guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: He now fell attacking the Chang Gate; his son Yi succeeded him as guard commander.

sentences.zh: 胡深，字仲淵，處州龍泉人。

translations.literal: Hu Shen, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was a man of Longquan in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shen, styled Zhongyuan, was from Longquan in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 穎異有智略，通經史百家之學。

translations.literal: Outstanding and unusual in talent, with strategy and counsel, he mastered the learning of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and resourceful, he was versed in the classics, histories, and the various schools of thought.

sentences.zh: 元末兵亂，嘆曰：「浙東地氣盡白，禍將及矣。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, when soldiers ravaged the land, he sighed and said: "The qi of the eastern Zhe region has turned wholly white; calamity is about to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: As Yuan armies ravaged the realm he sighed: "The eastern Zhe lands have turned deathly pale—disaster is near."

sentences.zh: 」乃集里中子弟自保。

translations.literal: " He thereupon gathered the young men of the village to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He then rallied the young men of his district for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 石抹宜孫以萬戶鎮處州，辟參軍事，募兵數千，收捕諸山寇。

translations.literal: Shimo Yisun, as chiliarch of ten thousand households, garrisoned Chuzhou; he recruited Shen as staff for military affairs, raised several thousand troops, and captured and subdued the mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shimo Yisun, holding Chuzhou as chiliarch, took Shen onto his staff, raised several thousand men, and suppressed mountain bandits.

sentences.zh: 溫州韓虎等殺主將叛。

translations.literal: In Wenzhou, Han Hu and others killed their commanding general and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenzhou, Han Hu and others murdered their commander and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 深往諭之，軍民感泣，殺虎以城降。

translations.literal: Shen went to admonish them; soldiers and civilians wept with emotion, killed Hu, and submitted the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shen went to reason with them; troops and people were moved to tears, slew Hu, and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 已，偕章溢討龍泉之亂，搜旁縣盜，以次平之。

translations.literal: Afterward, together with Zhang Yi he campaigned against the disorder in Longquan, searched out bandits in neighboring counties, and pacified them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Zhang Yi, he quelled unrest in Longquan and swept neighboring counties of bandits in succession.

sentences.zh: 宜孫時已進行省參政，承製命深為元帥。

translations.literal: Yisun had by then been promoted to provincial administrator; by imperial commission he appointed Shen marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun had risen to provincial administrator and, by imperial order, appointed Shen marshal.

sentences.zh: 戊戌十二月，太祖親征婺州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the year wuxu the Founding Emperor personally campaigned against Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of wuxu the founding emperor marched in person against Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 深帥兵車數百輛往援，至松溪不能救，敗去，婺遂下。

translations.literal: Shen led several hundred war carts to relieve it; reaching Songxi he could not save the city, was defeated and withdrew, and Wuzhou thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: Shen led hundreds of war carts to its relief, but at Songxi could not break through, was beaten back, and Wuzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 明年，耿再成侵處州，宜孫分遣元帥葉琛、參謀林彬祖、鎮撫陳中真及深帥兵拒戰。

translations.literal: The next year Geng Zaichang invaded Chuzhou; Yisun separately dispatched the marshals Ye Chen, the staff officer Lin Binzu, the garrison commissioner Chen Zhongzhen, and Shen to lead troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Geng Zaichang invaded Chuzhou; Yisun sent marshals Ye Chen, adviser Lin Binzu, commissioner Chen Zhongzhen, and Shen to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 會胡大海兵至，與再成合，大破之，進抵城下。

translations.literal: When Hu Dahai's troops arrived, they united with Zaichang, inflicted a great defeat, and advanced to the foot of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dahai's force joined Zaichang, routed the defenders, and pressed to the walls.

sentences.zh: 宜孫戰敗，與葉琛、章溢走建寧，處州遂下。

translations.literal: Yisun was defeated in battle; together with Ye Chen and Zhang Yi he fled to Jianning, and Chuzhou thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun was defeated and fled with Ye Chen and Zhang Yi to Jianning; Chuzhou was taken.

sentences.zh: 深以龍泉、慶元、松陽、遂昌四縣降。

translations.literal: Shen submitted with the four counties of Longquan, Qingyuan, Songyang, and Suichang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen surrendered with Longquan, Qingyuan, Songyang, and Suichang.

sentences.zh: 太祖素知深名，召見，授左司員外郎，遣還處州。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had long known Shen's name; he summoned and received him, appointed him Outer Vice Director of the Left Secretariat, and sent him back to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor, who had long known Shen's reputation, received him, made him outer vice director of the left secretariat, and sent him back to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 招集部曲，從征江西。

translations.literal: He gathered his followers and followed the campaign in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his followers and joined the Jiangxi campaign.

sentences.zh: 既定，命以親軍指揮守吉安。

translations.literal: When it was settled, he was ordered to guard Ji'an with his personal guard as commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the region was secured he was ordered to hold Ji'an with his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 處州苗軍叛，殺守將耿再成，深從平章邵榮討誅之。

translations.literal: The Miao troops of Chuzhou rebelled and killed the garrison commander Geng Zaichang; Shen followed the Pacification Commissioner Shao Rong in campaigning to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuzhou's Miao troops rebelled and killed Geng Zaichang, Shen joined Pacification Commissioner Shao Rong in suppressing them.

sentences.zh: 會改中書分省為浙東行中書省，遂以深為行省左右司郎中，總制處州軍民事。

translations.literal: It happened that the Branch Secretariat was changed to the Eastern Zhe Branch Secretariat; Shen was therefore made Left and Right Secretariat Director of the branch secretariat, with overall charge of military and civil affairs in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the branch secretariat became the Eastern Zhe branch secretariat, Shen was made its left and right director, governing Chuzhou's military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 時山寇竊發，人情未固，深募兵萬餘人，捕誅渠帥。

translations.literal: At the time mountain bandits rose in secret and popular sentiment was not yet firm; Shen recruited more than ten thousand troops and captured and executed the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: With bandits still active and the people unsettled, he raised more than ten thousand men and executed the chief rebels.

sentences.zh: 沿海軍素驍，誅其尤橫者數人，患遂息。

translations.literal: The coastal troops were by nature fierce; he executed several of the most overbearing among them, and the trouble thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal troops were notoriously unruly; he put several of the worst to death and the trouble subsided.

sentences.zh: 癸卯九月，諸全叛將謝再興以張士誠兵犯東陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the year guimao the rebel general of Zhugu Xie Zaixing brought Zhang Shicheng's troops to invade Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In guimao, ninth month, the Zhugu rebel Xie Zaixing led Zhang Shicheng's army against Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 左丞李文忠令深引兵為前鋒，再興敗走。

translations.literal: The Left Chancellor Li Wenzhong ordered Shen to lead troops as vanguard; Zaixing was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Li Wenzhong sent Shen ahead as vanguard; Zaixing was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 深建議以諸全為浙東籓屏，乃度地去諸全五十里並五指山築新城，分兵戍守。

translations.literal: Shen proposed making Zhugu a screen for eastern Zhe; he therefore measured ground fifty li from Zhugu and at Wuzhi Mountain built a new city, dividing troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen urged that Zhugu serve as eastern Zhe's bulwark; he surveyed a site fifty li away at Wuzhi Mountain, built a new city, and posted garrisons.

sentences.zh: 太祖初聞再興叛，急馳使詣文忠，別為城守計。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor first heard of Zaixing's rebellion, he urgently dispatched a messenger to Wenzhong with separate plans for city defense.
translations.idiomatic: On first hearing of Zaixing's revolt, the founding emperor urgently sent orders to Wenzhong for alternate defenses.

sentences.zh: 至則工已竣。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the work was already finished.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the messenger arrived, the new fortifications were already complete.

sentences.zh: 後士誠將李伯升大舉來侵，頓新城下，不能拔，敗去。

translations.literal: Later Shicheng's general Li Bosheng came in force to invade; he halted below the new city, could not take it, and was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Bosheng led a great invasion, camped beneath the new city, failed to take it, and withdrew defeated.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉深功，賜以名馬。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor praised Shen's merit and bestowed a famous horse on him.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor commended Shen's achievement and gave him a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱吳王，以深為王府參軍，仍守處州。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor assumed the title King of Wu, he made Shen a staff officer of the princely establishment, while he still guarded Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor took the title King of Wu, Shen became a staff officer of the princely household while continuing to hold Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 溫州豪周宗道聚眾據平陽。

translations.literal: The magnate Zhou Zongdao of Wenzhou gathered a crowd and held Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wenzhou strongman Zhou Zongdao raised followers and seized Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 數為方國珍從子明善所逼，以城來歸。

translations.literal: Many times pressed by Fang Guozhen's nephew Mingshan, he submitted the city.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly harried by Fang Guozhen's nephew Mingshan, he surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 明善怒，攻之。

translations.literal: Mingshan was enraged and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan, enraged, attacked him.

sentences.zh: 深遣兵擊走明善，遂下瑞安，進兵溫州。

translations.literal: Shen sent troops, drove Mingshan off, thereupon took Ruian, and advanced his army to Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen sent troops, routed Mingshan, took Ruian, and marched on Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 方氏懼，請歲輸銀三萬充軍實。

translations.literal: The Fang clan were afraid and requested to pay thirty thousand taels of silver yearly to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Fang clan, alarmed, offered thirty thousand taels of silver yearly for military supplies.

sentences.zh: 乃命深班師，復還鎮。

translations.literal: He was therefore ordered to withdraw the army and return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was ordered to withdraw and resume his garrison.

sentences.zh: 陳友定兵至，破之，追至浦城，又敗其守兵，城遂下。

translations.literal: When Chen Youding's troops arrived, he defeated them, pursued to Pucheng, again defeated the garrison troops, and the city thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youding advanced, Shen defeated him, pursued to Pucheng, routed the garrison, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 進拔松溪，獲其守將張子玉。

translations.literal: He advanced to take Songxi and captured its garrison commander Zhang Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Songxi and captured the commander Zhang Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 因請發廣信、撫州、建昌三路兵，規取八閩。

translations.literal: He therefore requested to mobilize the troops of the three routes of Guangxin, Fuzhou, and Jianchang to plan the seizure of the Eight Min regions.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to raise the armies of Guangxin, Fuzhou, and Jianchang for a campaign to seize Fujian.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜曰：「子玉驍將，擒之則友定破膽。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was pleased and said: "Ziyu is a fierce general; once he is captured, Youding will lose heart."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor rejoiced: "Ziyu is a fierce commander—capture him and Youding's courage will break."

sentences.zh: 乘勢攻之，理無不克。

translations.literal: Press the attack while the momentum holds, and by reason there is none that cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Strike while the advantage holds, and success is assured."

sentences.zh: 」因命廣信指揮硃亮祖由鉛山、建昌，左丞王溥由杉關，會深齊進。

translations.literal: " He therefore ordered the Guangxin commander Zhu Liangzu to advance by Qianshan and Jianchang, the Left Chancellor Wang Pu by Shan Pass, and to join Shen in a united advance.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhu Liangzu from Guangxin via Qianshan and Jianchang, Left Chancellor Wang Pu via Shan Pass, to advance with Shen in concert.

sentences.zh: 已，亮祖等克崇安，進攻建寧。

translations.literal: Before long Liangzu and the others took Chong'an and advanced to attack Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liangzu took Chong'an and moved against Jianning.

sentences.zh: 友定將阮德柔固守。

translations.literal: Youding's general Ruan Derou held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Youding's general Ruan Derou defended stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 深視氛祲不利，欲緩之。

translations.literal: Shen viewed the omens as unfavorable and wished to slow the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Shen read the signs as ill-omened and urged delay.

sentences.zh: 亮祖曰：「師已至此，庸可緩乎？

translations.literal: Liangzu said: "The army has already come this far—how can it be slowed?"
translations.idiomatic: Liangzu said: "We have come this far—how can we hold back?"

sentences.zh: 且天道幽遠，山澤之氣變態無常，何足征也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Way of Heaven is obscure and far; the vapors of mountains and marshes change without constancy—what is there worth taking as omen?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's ways are inscrutable; mountain mists shift without pattern—what omens can bind us?"

sentences.zh: 」時德柔兵屯錦江，逼深陣後。

translations.literal: " At the time Derou's troops were encamped on the Jin River, pressing on the rear of Shen's formation.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Derou's force lay on the Jin River, threatening Shen's rear.

sentences.zh: 亮祖督戰益急。

translations.literal: Liangzu pressed the fighting all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzu drove the battle ever harder.

sentences.zh: 深引兵還擊，破其二柵。

translations.literal: Shen led troops in a counterattack and broke two of their palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Shen wheeled about and smashed two enemy stockades.

sentences.zh: 德柔軍力戰，友定自以銳師夾擊。

translations.literal: Derou's army fought fiercely; Youding himself brought elite troops to strike from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Derou's men fought desperately; Youding himself led crack troops in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 日已暮，深突圍走，馬蹶被執，遂遇害，年五十二。

translations.literal: The day was already dusk; Shen broke through the encirclement and fled; his horse stumbled and he was captured, and he thereupon met his death, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Shen broke out of the encirclement; his horse fell, he was taken, and killed—aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 追封縉雲郡伯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Jinyun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗問宋濂曰：「胡深何如人？

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor once asked Song Lian: "What sort of man is Hu Shen?"
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor once asked Song Lian: "What manner of man is Hu Shen?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「文武才也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "A talent in both civil and military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Song Lian answered: "A man of both civil and military gifts."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「誠然。

translations.literal: " The Founding Emperor said: "Truly so."
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor said: "That is true."

sentences.zh: 浙東一障，吾方賴之。

translations.literal: Eastern Zhe is one barrier—I am just now relying on him."
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhe is my shield—I depend on him now."

sentences.zh: 」而深以久任鄉郡，志圖平閩以報效，竟以死徇。

translations.literal: " Yet Shen, because he long held his native commandery, set his heart on pacifying Min to repay his obligation, and in the end died in fulfillment of that loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, long governing his home region, had resolved to pacify Fujian in loyal service—and died in that cause.

sentences.zh: 深馭眾寬厚，用兵十餘年，未嘗妄戮一人。

translations.literal: Shen governed the multitude with generous kindness; in more than ten years of campaigning he never wantonly killed a single person.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled his men with generosity; in more than ten years of war he never executed a man without cause.

sentences.zh: 守處州，興學造士。

translations.literal: While guarding Chuzhou he promoted learning and nurtured scholars.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Chuzhou he fostered schools and cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 縉雲田稅重，以新沒入田租償其數。

translations.literal: The land tax in Jinyun was heavy; he used rents from newly confiscated fields to make up the amount.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyun's grain levy was burdensome; he offset it with rents from newly seized estates.

sentences.zh: 鹽稅什一，請半取之，以通商賈。

translations.literal: The salt tax was one in ten; he requested to take only half, so as to open commerce.
translations.idiomatic: The salt levy stood at ten percent; he halved it to revive trade.

sentences.zh: 軍民皆懷其惠雲。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians alike cherished his kindness—thus it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians alike cherished his kindness—so it was said.

sentences.zh: 孫興祖

translations.literal: Sun Xingzu
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingzu

sentences.zh: 孫興祖，濠人。

translations.literal: Sun Xingzu was a man of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xingzu was a native of Hao.

sentences.zh: 從太祖渡江，積功為都先鋒。

translations.literal: He followed the Founding Emperor in crossing the Yangzi and through accumulated merit became Chief Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi with the founding emperor and rose by merit to chief vanguard.

sentences.zh: 戰龍江，遷統軍元帥。

translations.literal: In the battle on the Long River he was transferred to marshal commanding armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the Long River battle he was promoted to army marshal.

sentences.zh: 破瑞昌八陣營，擢天策衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He broke the Eight-Formation camps at Ruichang and was elevated to commander of the Tiance Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered the Eight-Formation camps at Ruichang and was made commander of the Tiance Guard.

sentences.zh: 興祖沉毅有謀，大將軍徐達雅重之。

translations.literal: Xingzu was deep, resolute, and resourceful; the Grand General Xu Da greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Steady and shrewd, Xingzu won the high regard of Grand General Xu Da.

sentences.zh: 克泰州，以達請，命守海陵。

translations.literal: When Taizhou was taken, at Da's request he was ordered to guard Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizhou fell, at Xu Da's request he was posted to Hailing.

sentences.zh: 海陵，士誠兵入淮要地也。

translations.literal: Hailing was a vital point where Shicheng's troops entered the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was the key gateway through which Zhang Shicheng's forces entered the Huai.

sentences.zh: 興祖整軍令，練士伍，防禦甚嚴。

translations.literal: Xingzu tightened military law, drilled the ranks, and defended with great strictness.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu enforced discipline, drilled his men, and held the post with iron rigor.

sentences.zh: 吳兵自海口來侵，擊敗之，擒彭元帥。

translations.literal: Wu troops invaded from the sea mouth; he defeated them and captured Marshal Peng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu forces came from the estuary he routed them and took Marshal Peng prisoner.

sentences.zh: 平江既下，命興祖取通州，士誠守將已詣徐達降。

translations.literal: After Pingjiang had fallen, he was ordered to take Tongzhou; Shicheng's garrison commander had already gone to Xu Da to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Pingjiang fell he was sent to take Tongzhou; Zhang Shicheng's commander had already surrendered to Xu Da.

sentences.zh: 進大都督府副使，移鎮彭城。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice director of the Chief Military Commission and transferred to garrison Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the chief military commission and was shifted to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 達既定關陝，旋師北向，檄興祖會東昌。

translations.literal: When Da had settled Shaanxi and Gansu, he turned his army northward and summoned Xingzu to join him at Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: After securing Shaanxi and Gansu, Xu Da marched north and called Xingzu to Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 從克元都。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of the Yuan capital.
translations.idiomatic: He joined in the capture of the Yuan capital.

sentences.zh: 置燕山六衛，留兵三萬人，命興祖守之，領大都督分府事。

translations.literal: The six guards of Yan Mountain were established; thirty thousand troops were left behind, and Xingzu was ordered to guard them and to head the branch office of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Six Yan Mountain guards were established; thirty thousand men were left under Xingzu, who also headed the branch chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 大兵西征，擴廓由居庸窺北平。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned westward, Kökö Temür peered at Beiping through Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army campaigned westward, Kökö Temür threatened Beiping through Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 達謂諸將：「北平有孫都督，不足慮。

translations.literal: Da told the generals: "Beiping has Regional Commander Sun—there is no need for worry."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da told his officers: "Beiping has Commander Sun—we need not worry."

sentences.zh: 」遂直搗太原。

translations.literal: " He thereupon drove straight at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck straight for Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 語詳《達傳》。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of Da.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Xu Da's biography.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，帥六衛卒從達出塞，次三不剌川，遇敵，力戰死，年三十五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he led the troops of the six guards, followed Da beyond the frontier, halted at the Sanbulachuan, encountered the enemy, fought fiercely, and died, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 he led the six guards beyond the frontier with Xu Da, halted at Sanbulachuan, met the enemy, and was killed in fierce fighting—aged thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 太祖悼惜之，追封燕山侯，諡忠愍，配享通州常遇春祠。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor mourned and prized him, posthumously enfeoffing him as Marquis of Yan Mountain, with the posthumous title Zhongmin, and granting him attendant worship in Chang Yuchun's shrine at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor mourned him, posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yan Mountain with the posthumous name Zhongmin, and granted him a place in Chang Yuchun's shrine at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，中書省以都督同知汪興祖兼俸事入奏。

translations.literal: Before long the Secretariat of State, because Regional Commander Tongzhi Wang Xingzu was entering court on combined stipend business, memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the secretariat reported that Regional Commander Tongzhi Wang Xingzu had come to court on a joint stipend matter.

sentences.zh: 帝聞奏興祖名，嘆息，命以月俸給故燕山侯興祖家。

translations.literal: The emperor heard the name Xingzu in the memorial, sighed, and ordered that the monthly stipend be given to the household of the late Marquis of Yan Mountain, Xingzu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the name Xingzu, the emperor sighed and ordered the monthly stipend paid to the household of the late Marquis Sun Xingzu.

sentences.zh: 以其長子恪襲武德衛指揮使。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ke inherited the post of commander of the Wude Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ke succeeded as commander of the Wude Guard.

sentences.zh: 久之，歷都督僉事。

translations.literal: After a long time he rose through offices to be a commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In time he rose to commissioner of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以右參將從藍玉北征，至捕魚兒海。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, as right deputy general he followed Lan Yu on the northern expedition, reaching Buyur Lake.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21, as right deputy general he joined Lan Yu's northern expedition to Buyur Lake.

sentences.zh: 論功封全寧侯，歲祿二千石，予世券。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Quanning with an annual stipend of two thousand piculs of grain and a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Quanning, with two thousand piculs yearly and a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 恪謹敏，有儒將風。

translations.literal: Ke was cautious and quick-witted, with the bearing of a scholar-general.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was prudent and alert, with the manner of a scholar-general.

sentences.zh: 從征楚、蜀，還駐沔陽，簡閱各衛所軍士備邊。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns in Chu and Shu, returned to garrison at Mianyang, and inspected the troops of the guards and battalions to prepare the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Chu and Shu, then garrisoned Mianyang and reviewed frontier troops of the guards and battalions.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，進兼太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was advanced to concurrent Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he was made concurrent Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，籍兵山西，從宋國公勝練兵。

translations.literal: Before long he registered troops in Shanxi and followed the Duke of Song, Sheng, in drilling soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was registering troops in Shanxi and drilling soldiers under Duke Song Sheng.

sentences.zh: 旋召還，賜第中都。

translations.literal: He was soon recalled, and a mansion in the central capital was bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and given a residence in the central capital.

sentences.zh: 後坐藍玉黨死。

translations.literal: Later he was put to death as a member of Lan Yu's faction.
translations.idiomatic: He was later executed as an associate of Lan Yu's faction.

sentences.zh: 曹良臣

translations.literal: Cao Liangchen
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liangchen

sentences.zh: 曹良臣，安豐人。

translations.literal: Cao Liangchen was a man of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liangchen was a native of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 潁寇起，聚鄉里築堡自固。

translations.literal: When bandits rose along the Ying River, he gathered the countryside, built a fort, and held himself secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying River bandits rose, he rallied his neighbors, fortified a stronghold, and held out.

sentences.zh: 歸太祖於應天，為江淮行省參政。

translations.literal: He submitted to the Founding Emperor at Yingtian and was made provincial administrator of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted at Yingtian and was made provincial administrator of the Jiang-Huai branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從取淮東，收浙西，進行省左丞。

translations.literal: He followed in the taking of eastern Huai and the recovery of western Zhe, and was promoted to Left Vice Administrator of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take eastern Huai and western Zhe and was promoted to left vice administrator of the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從大軍取元都，略地至澤、潞。

translations.literal: He followed the great army in taking the Yuan capital and extended operations to Ze and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the capture of the Yuan capital and extended operations to Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 進山西行省平章，還守通州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Shanxi Branch Secretariat and returned to guard Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became pacification commissioner of the Shanxi branch secretariat and returned to guard Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時大兵出山西，通州守備單弱，所部不滿千人。

translations.literal: At the time the great army had gone out into Shanxi; the defenses at Tongzhou were thin and weak, and the troops under his command numbered fewer than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With the main army in Shanxi, Tongzhou's defenses were thin—he had fewer than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 元丞相也速將萬騎營白河。

translations.literal: The Yuan Chancellor Ayushiridara led ten thousand horsemen and encamped on the White River.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chancellor Ayushiridara camped on the White River with ten thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 良臣曰：「吾兵少，不可與戰。

translations.literal: Liangchen said: "Our troops are few and we cannot fight them."
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen said: "We are too few to fight."

sentences.zh: 彼眾雖多，亡國之余，敗氣不振，當以計走之。

translations.literal: " Though they are many, they are the remnant of a perished state; their defeated spirit does not rise—we should use a stratagem to drive them off."
translations.idiomatic: Though numerous, they are a defeated remnant of a fallen dynasty—strategy can drive them off."

sentences.zh: 」乃密遣指揮仵勇等於瀕河舟中多立赤幟，亙三十余里，鉦鼓聲相聞。

translations.literal: " He thereupon secretly sent the commander Wu Yong and others to set up many red banners on boats along the riverbank, stretching more than thirty li, with the sound of gongs and drums heard one from another.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent Commander Wu Yong to line boats along the river with red banners for thirty li, gongs and drums sounding without cease.

sentences.zh: 也速大駭，遁去。

translations.literal: Ayushiridara was greatly terrified and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Ayushiridara was terrified and fled.

sentences.zh: 良臣出精騎逐交百余里，元兵自是不敢窺北平。

translations.literal: Liangchen sent out elite cavalry in pursuit for more than a hundred li; from then on the Yuan troops did not dare peer at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He sent elite cavalry in pursuit for a hundred li; thereafter Yuan forces dared not threaten Beiping.

sentences.zh: 復從大將軍達擊擴廓帖木兒於定西，敗之。

translations.literal: He again followed the Grand General Da in attacking Kökö Temür at Dingxi and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Grand General Xu Da against Kökö Temür at Dingxi and routed him.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年封宣寧侯，歲祿九百石，予世券。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanning with an annual stipend of nine hundred piculs of grain and a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xuanning, with nine hundred piculs yearly and a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 明年從伐蜀，克歸州山寨，取容美諸土司。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the campaign against Shu, took the mountain stockades of Guizhou, and seized the native chieftains of Rongmei and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he campaigned in Shu, took Guizhou's mountain strongholds, and subdued the Rongmei chieftains.

sentences.zh: 會周德興拔茅岡覃垕寨，自白鹽山伐木開道，出紙坊溪以趨夔州，進克重慶。

translations.literal: When Zhou Dexing took the Qinhao stockade at Maogang, from Baiyan Mountain they felled timber to open a road, came out at Zhifang Stream to press toward Kuizhou, and advanced to take Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Dexing took the Qinhao stockade at Maogang, timber was cut at Baiyan Mountain to open a road through Zhifang Stream toward Kuizhou, and Chongqing was taken.

sentences.zh: 明年從副將軍文忠北征，至臚朐河，收其部籓。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the Deputy General Wenzhong on the northern expedition, reaching the Luchuan River, and received submission from its dependent tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined Deputy General Wenzhong's northern expedition to the Luchuan River and received the submission of its tribes.

sentences.zh: 文忠帥良臣持二十日糧，兼程進至土剌河。

translations.literal: Wenzhong led Liangchen with twenty days' grain, marched day and night, and advanced to the Tula River.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong led Liangchen with twenty days' rations, marched night and day, and reached the Tula River.

sentences.zh: 哈剌章渡河拒戰，少卻。

translations.literal: Qaračan crossed the river to resist; he was slightly driven back.
translations.idiomatic: Qaračan crossed the river to resist and was driven back.

sentences.zh: 追至阿魯渾河，敵騎大集。

translations.literal: They pursued to the Aruhun River; the enemy cavalry gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached the Aruhun River, where enemy cavalry massed.

sentences.zh: 將士皆殊死戰，敵大敗走，而良臣與指揮周顯、常榮、張耀皆戰死。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers all fought to the death; the enemy were greatly defeated and fled, yet Liangchen, together with the commanders Zhou Xian, Chang Rong, and Zhang Yao, all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men fought to the death; the enemy was routed, but Liangchen with Zhou Xian, Chang Rong, and Zhang Yao all fell.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈良臣安國公，諡忠壯，列祀功臣廟。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Liangchen was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Anguo, with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang, and his tablet was placed in the Shrine of Meritorious Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death Liangchen was posthumously made Duke of Anguo, posthumous name Zhongzhuang, and honored in the Shrine of Meritorious Ministers.

sentences.zh: 子泰襲侯，坐藍玉黨死，爵除。

translations.literal: His son Tai inherited the marquisate; he was put to death as a member of Lan Yu's faction, and the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tai inherited the marquisate but was executed in Lan Yu's faction case and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 附 周顯 常榮 張耀

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhou Xian, Chang Rong, Zhang Yao
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhou Xian, Chang Rong, and Zhang Yao

sentences.zh: 顯，合肥人。

translations.literal: Xian was a man of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xian was from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，累功至指揮同知。

translations.literal: He followed the crossing of the Yangzi and through accumulated merit rose to vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi with the founding armies and rose to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，以收應昌紅羅山寨，遷指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, for recovering the Red Luo mountain stockade at Yingchang, he was transferred to commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 3, for taking the Red Luo stockade at Yingchang, he was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 榮，開平王遇春再從弟，歷指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Rong was a second cousin once removed of the Prince of Kaiping, Yuchun, and rose through offices to be a commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Rong was a second cousin of Prince of Kaiping Chang Yuchun and rose to commissioner of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 遇春卒於軍，榮護喪還。

translations.literal: When Yuchun died in the army, Rong escorted the coffin back.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchun died on campaign, Rong escorted his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 從硃亮祖平蜀，累官至振武衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: He followed Zhu Liangzu in pacifying Shu and through accumulated offices rose to vice commander of the Zhenwu Guard.
