translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhu Liangzu in pacifying Shu and rose to vice commander of the Zhenwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 耀，壽州人，初從陳埜先。

translations.literal: Yao was a man of Shouzhou; at first he followed Chen Yexian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yao was from Shouzhou and had first served Chen Yexian.

sentences.zh: 建康下，始歸附。

translations.literal: When Jiankang fell, he first came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was taken he submitted.

sentences.zh: 累功為守御福建指揮使，守興化。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he became commander of the Fujian Defense Command, guarding Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: By merit he became commander of the Fujian defense command and held Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 至是俱戰沒，帝厚恤諸臣家，命有司各表其墓。

translations.literal: On this occasion they all died in battle; the emperor richly compensated the families of the ministers and ordered the authorities to mark out each of their tombs.
translations.idiomatic: All three fell in this battle; the emperor generously compensated their families and ordered their graves marked.

sentences.zh: 濮英，廬州人。

translations.literal: Pu Ying was a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Ying was a native of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 初以勇力為百夫長，積功至西安衛指揮。

translations.literal: At first, through courage and strength he became a centurion, and through accumulated merit rose to commander of the Xi'an Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a centurion through sheer valor and rose to commander of the Xi'an Guard.

sentences.zh: 坐軍政不修，召還詰責，遣葉升代之。

translations.literal: He was demoted for failure to maintain military administration, recalled and rebuked, and Ye Sheng was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: For lax military administration he was recalled and rebuked; Ye Sheng was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 升更言其賢，令還衛。

translations.literal: Sheng further reported on his worthiness, and he was ordered to return to the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then praised his merit, and he was ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 洪武十九年，太祖命耿炳文選陝西都司衛所卒備邊，惟英所練稱勁旅，加都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Hongwu the Founding Emperor ordered Geng Bingwen to select troops from the guards and battalions of the Shaanxi command for frontier defense; only those trained by Ying were called a crack force, and he was added as Commissioner of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 19 Geng Bingwen selected Shaanxi garrison troops for the frontier; only Ying's men were judged elite, and he was made commissioner of the chief military commission.

sentences.zh: 明年命師所部隨大將軍馮勝北征。

translations.literal: The next year he was ordered to lead his division and follow the Grand General Feng Sheng on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he led his command under Grand General Feng Sheng on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 抵金山，降納哈出，遂班師，而以英將奇兵三千人為殿。

translations.literal: Reaching Jin Mountain, they received the submission of Naghachu, then withdrew the army, while Ying led three thousand picked troops as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: At Jin Mountain they accepted Naghachu's surrender and withdrew; Ying led three thousand picked men as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 納哈出余眾竄匿者尚數十萬，聞帥旋，設伏於途，謀俟大軍過竄取之。

translations.literal: Naghachu's remnant followers still in hiding numbered several hundred thousand; hearing that the main army was withdrawing, they set an ambush on the road, planning to wait until the great army had passed and then spring out to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Naghachu's hidden remnants still numbered hundreds of thousands; learning the main army was withdrawing, they ambushed the road, intending to strike once it had passed.

sentences.zh: 未發。

translations.literal: They had not yet struck.
translations.idiomatic: The trap had not yet been sprung.

sentences.zh: 英後至，猝為所乘，衝突不能出，馬踣，遂見執。

translations.literal: Ying came up behind, was suddenly caught by them, charged but could not break out, his horse fell, and he was thereupon captured.
translations.idiomatic: Ying came up last, was suddenly trapped, could not break through, his horse fell, and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 敵既得英，思挾為質。

translations.literal: Once the enemy had obtained Ying, they thought to hold him as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, having captured Ying, meant to hold him hostage.

sentences.zh: 英絕食不言，乘間引佩刀剖腹死。

translations.literal: Ying refused food and would not speak; seizing an interval he drew his belt dagger and disemboweled himself to die.
translations.idiomatic: Ying starved himself in silence, then seized a moment to draw his dagger and cut open his belly.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈金山侯，諡忠襄。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Jin Mountain, with the posthumous title Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death he was posthumously made Marquis of Jin Mountain, posthumous name Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 明年進贈樂浪公。

translations.literal: The next year he was further posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was further posthumously made Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 封其子璵為西涼侯，祿二千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: His son Yu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiliang with a stipend of twenty-five hundred piculs of grain and a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiliang with twenty-five hundred piculs yearly and a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，命練兵東昌，又令駐臨清，訓練士卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was ordered to drill troops at Dongchang, and again ordered to garrison at Linqing to train soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he was ordered to drill troops at Dongchang and garrison Linqing to train the army.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，召還，同宋國公勝等簡閱山西士馬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was recalled, and together with the Duke of Song, Sheng, and others inspected the soldiers and horses of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 he was recalled to join Duke Song Sheng in reviewing Shanxi troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 璵能修父職，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Yu was able to fulfill his father's duties; the emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu proved able to carry on his father's work; the emperor greatly commended him.

sentences.zh: 復令籍山西民兵，所籍州縣最多，事集而不擾。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to register militia in Shanxi; among the prefectures and counties registered, his assignment was the largest, yet the work was completed without disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to register Shanxi militia—the largest assignment of any—and completed it without disorder.

sentences.zh: 明年坐藍玉黨，戍五開死。

translations.literal: The next year he was condemned as a member of Lan Yu's faction, exiled to Wukai, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was implicated in Lan Yu's faction, exiled to Wukai, and died in banishment.

sentences.zh: 洪武中指揮使死事者，又有于光、嚴德、孫虎。

translations.literal: Among guard commanders who died in service during the Hongwu reign were also Yu Guang, Yan De, and Sun Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Other guard commanders who died in service in the Hongwu era included Yu Guang, Yan De, and Sun Hu.

sentences.zh: 附 于光 等

translations.literal: Appendix: Yu Guang and others
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Yu Guang and others

sentences.zh: 光，都昌人。

translations.literal: Guang was a man of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Guang was from Duchang.

sentences.zh: 初事徐壽輝，鎮浮梁。

translations.literal: At first he served Xu Shouhui and garrisoned Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served Xu Shouhui and garrisoned Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒弒壽輝，光以浮梁來降，授樞密院判。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang murdered Shouhui; Guang submitted Fuliang and was appointed a judge of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang murdered Shouhui, Guang surrendered Fuliang and was made a privy council judge.

sentences.zh: 積功為鷹揚衛指揮，鎮鞏昌。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he became commander of the Yingyang Guard and garrisoned Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: By merit he became commander of the Yingyang Guard and held Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 擴廓圍蘭州，光赴援至馬蘭灘，戰敗被執。

translations.literal: Kökö Temür besieged Lanzhou; Guang went to relieve it, reached Malan Shoals, was defeated in battle, and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Kökö Temür besieged Lanzhou, Guang marched to relieve it, was beaten at Malan Shoals, and captured.

sentences.zh: 以徇城下。

translations.literal: He was displayed before the city as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He was paraded beneath the walls to intimidate the garrison.

sentences.zh: 光大呼曰：「公等但堅守，徐將軍將大軍旦夕至矣！

translations.literal: Guang cried out loudly: "You gentlemen need only hold firm—General Xu will bring the great army within the day!"
translations.idiomatic: Guang shouted: "Hold the city—General Xu will bring the main army any day now!"

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，批其頰，遂被殺，祀功臣廟。

translations.literal: " The bandits were enraged, struck his cheeks, and he was thereupon killed; he is worshipped in the Shrine of Meritorious Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, enraged, beat his face and killed him; he is honored in the Shrine of Meritorious Ministers.

sentences.zh: 嚴德，太平人。

translations.literal: Yan De was a man of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yan De was from Taiping.

sentences.zh: 從起兵，積功為海寧衛指揮。

translations.literal: He followed the rising of the army and through accumulated merit became commander of the Haining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the founding armies and rose to commander of the Haining Guard.

sentences.zh: 從硃亮祖討方國珍，戰歿於台州。

translations.literal: He followed Zhu Liangzu in campaigning against Fang Guozhen and died in battle at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhu Liangzu against Fang Guozhen and was killed at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 追封天水郡公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 孫虎，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Sun Hu—of what place he was is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hu's native place is unknown.

sentences.zh: 從援池州，下於潛、昌化，定建德、諸全，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed in the relief of Chizhou, took Yuqian and Changhua, and pacified Jiande and Zhugu, all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He helped relieve Chizhou, took Yuqian and Changhua, and helped secure Jiande and Zhugu.

sentences.zh: 授千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 克新城、桐、廬，進海寧衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He took Xincheng, Tong, and Lu, and was advanced to commander of the Haining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Xincheng, Tong, and Lu and was promoted to commander of the Haining Guard.

sentences.zh: 平嘉興盜。

translations.literal: He pacified the bandits of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified bandits in Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 從副將軍李文忠北征，由東道入應昌，至落馬河與元兵戰死。

translations.literal: He followed the Deputy General Wenzhong on the northern expedition, entered Yingchang by the eastern route, reached Luoma River, and died in battle with the Yuan troops.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Deputy General Wenzhong's northern expedition, entered Yingchang by the east, reached Luoma River, and was killed fighting Yuan forces.

sentences.zh: 追封康安郡伯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Kang'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Earl of Kang'an.

sentences.zh: 又指揮僉事劉廣，戍永平，禦寇戰死。

translations.literal: There was also the Commissioner Liu Guang, who garrisoned Yongping, defended against bandits, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Liu Guang, garrisoning Yongping, was killed repelling raiders.

sentences.zh: 涼州衛百戶劉林戍涼州，也先帖木兒叛，戰死。

translations.literal: The centurion Liu Lin of the Liangzhou Guard garrisoned Liangzhou; when Yexian Temür rebelled, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Centurion Liu Lin of the Liangzhou Guard was killed when Yexian Temür rebelled.

sentences.zh: 邊人壯之，名其所居竇融台為劉林台。

translations.literal: The frontier people admired his valor and renamed the place where he dwelt—the Dou Rong Terrace—as Liu Lin Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Border people admired his courage and renamed his post, the Dou Rong Terrace, as Liu Lin Terrace.

sentences.zh: 錢塘衛千戶袁興，全椒人。

translations.literal: The chiliarch Yuan Xing of the Qiantang Guard was a man of Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Chiliarch Yuan Xing of the Qiantang Guard was from Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 從征雲南，自請為前鋒，陷陣死。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Yunnan he volunteered to be vanguard, broke the enemy line, and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yunnan campaign he volunteered as vanguard, charged the enemy line, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 並褒贈有差。

translations.literal: They were all rewarded and enfeoffed in differing degrees.
translations.idiomatic: All received posthumous honors of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明祖之興，自決策渡江，始力爭於東南數千里之內，摧友諒，滅士誠，然後北定中原，南圖閩、粵，則廖永安胡大海以下諸人，厥功豈細哉！

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the rise of the Ming Founding Emperor, from the decision to cross the Yangzi he first strove within several thousand li of the southeast, shattered Youliang, destroyed Shicheng, and only then pacified the Central Plain in the north and turned south to plan Min and Yue—then the merit of Liao Yongan, Hu Dahai, and those below them: how could it be slight!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: From the decision to cross the Yangzi the Ming founder first fought across the southeast for thousands of li, broke Chen Youliang, destroyed Zhang Shicheng, and only then secured the north and turned to Fujian and Guangdong—men such as Liao Yongan and Hu Dahai below them: their service was no small thing!

sentences.zh: 計不旋踵，效命疆場，雖勛業未竟，然褒崇廟祀，竹帛爛然。

translations.literal: Without turning the heel, they gave their lives on the frontier; although their achievements were not brought to completion, yet they were exalted with temple sacrifice, and their names shine on silk and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: They turned at once to die on the battlefield; though their careers were cut short, temples and histories honor them, their names bright on scroll and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 以視功成命爵、終罹黨籍者，其猶幸也夫。

translations.literal: Compared with those who achieved success, received enfeoffment, and in the end fell into factional registers, they were perhaps still fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Beside those who won full glory and titles yet ended in factional purges, they may have been the more fortunate.
